8. CURRENT SOURCE FACTS

Fixture sequence at f14: snapshots() selects a request based on presence of a SystemUI window, detached/authority and a pending B, then clears all SystemUI visible IDs. inspectSurface first checks quickSignals, reads real windows, calls classifyDetailed with rootUnavailable/walkTruncated, takes a second actual INSPECTION-purpose system snapshot, then KeyguardCardVisibilityPolicy.decide returns the final inspected decision. beforeApply currently receives only request and decision. SystemUI presence is insufficient: system gates, foreign occlusion, credential/shade or incomplete roots may affect the result. A decision of HIDDEN_UNKNOWN is also insufficient by itself; reason and completeness are independent. The existing freeze report does not include req=10; optional formatting is not a reliable oracle. Stock processInspectionQueue waits for Main before taking the next non-stale read. The new code must move only an eligible read, with ordered application and fresh authority intact.

FluviKeyguardCardService processes Binder tree reads off Main and applies visibility on Main. In processInspectionQueue (~982), non-stale inspection waits in withContext(Dispatchers.Main.immediate) for applyInspection (~1494) before complete(active) can release a pending request. handleRecoverableSurface (~1702) reads pendingRequest, chooses a freshness obligation, preserves pending work while detached, or withdraws/reacquires after visible UNKNOWN. It must still observe the correct pending identity. The current policy performs a fresh system admission read at actual show/disclosure increase. Authority covers session, wake, visibility, interaction and attach generations. Existing terminal signals can withdraw without a successful tree walk.
The window owns addView, geometry, clicks, callbacks and removeView. prepareRetainedView may run before eligibility. settings.showFinancialDetails expresses preference, not permission for the next visible frame. Full/discreet is determined by current authorized presentation. Existing material controller chooses the isolated backend on its supported API/mode/animation path and can fall over to a Main-driven View. KeyguardOrbBufferRenderer retains custom slots, direct first apply and separate steady publication/retirement. On later R11 episodes the pressure route has no first-offer work. The old driver and the pressure clock must never be present in the default new path. KeyguardHeaderMaterialView contains the actual canonical scene/time/shader contract. Sharing immutable material descriptions is permitted; mutable shaders, Paint, Canvases or View instances must respect their thread owners.

9. PROVEN / UNPROVEN / MISSING

Fixture diagnosis PROVEN: the test commits to A before the actual classification/system decision is known, and the latest run stopped before the read-order assertion. Which particular underlying signal or classification disqualified request 10 is MISSING. UNPROVEN: the stock-vs-new read-ahead benefit on a real device, and whether this accounts for any single physical hitch. Do not “fix” visibility policy or shader behavior from the fixture exception. The user's physical result is partial subjective improvement on R11 with the symptom still present.

PROVEN: first-direct event ordering improved on R11's first retained episode; physical feedback rejected R11. Admission spent 135–251 ms after SCREEN_ON before SHOW on warm retained episodes. Later cycles ran the pressure View. Long intervals between CPU traversals and slow external event delivery exist. One direct send, a commit callback or publishing many buffers has not established smooth visible pixels. Previous controlled runs also demonstrate buffer-retention and independent-image-oracle problems in the legacy route.
UNPROVEN: how much the legacy multi-owner pipeline, Main traversal, shared HWUI/RenderThread/GPU scheduling, system wake/unlock transitions, diagnostics or service event delivery cause the perceived lag. In particular the three warm gaps cluster near withdrawal. The 182 ms callback-delivery delay does not prove a 182 ms covering bootstrap. OS events can arrive after the visual transition. No claim of a universal lag-free renderer or an Android timing guarantee.
MISSING: system wake/unlock visual start, physical first correct ORB, physical first sustained motion and last visible ORB on A142. Exact vsync/latch/present for these logs, early trustworthy emulator pixels, and a comparable baseline for stable locked intervals are missing. Normal final gates on R11 are missing. Obtain discriminating evidence with the repair in R12; do not request another unchanged R11 run.

10. ROOT-CAUSE OR FORENSIC GATE

Reviewer selection for this iteration: HF1 premature selection in the admission test, HF2 evidence loss and loose host matching, alongside the existing product hypotheses below. Correct HF1/HF2 by arming after real eligibility in a controlled detached service, validating the exact same A result, and saving same-attempt structured evidence. Falsification: if a proven qualifying A and a proven compatible B exist in the patched candidate yet B still cannot enter its real reader before A's ordered apply is released, that is a product scheduler failure. If the pair cannot be proved, the test verdict is FIXTURE_INVALID or EVIDENCE_MISSING. This distinction applies regardless of process exit code. Runtime read-ahead alone does not address warm captures already granted on their first inspection. Complete the single-surface rendering change.

Selected structural hypothesis H1: first/steady publication can depend on different owners and retained slots; the surviving fallback moves animation back to Main traversal. Removing app-owned buffer/fence bookkeeping and Main traversal from ongoing ORB motion, while keeping the first correct image ready and giving presentation one owner, will reduce post-admission delay or long visible gaps. Alternative H2: much of wake-to-visible is spent before authorization; a compatible next tree read can start sooner without changing when an answer is allowed to show anything. First R11 inspection finished at 1133947812, Main entered at 7899, next read started 7902. H2 addresses that exposed ordering dependency only, not system Binder latency. H3: visible unlock delay includes receipt of the first usable system signal and compositor removal. Immediate local revocation is in scope; changing platform admission criteria or guessing future unlock is outside scope. H4: OS scheduling, HWUI/driver/compositor or capture overhead can dominate across producers.
Precommitted interpretation: LEGACY versus SURFACE_LIVE under the same admission engine tests H1. SURFACE_STATIC versus SURFACE_LIVE isolates the incremental animation path with identical window, gate and first pixels. Stock R11 plus on/off read-ahead in an instrumented identical dispatcher tests H2. Separate locked steady motion and unlock-aligned samples discriminates H3/H4. A punctual producer with stale composed frames moves the investigation downstream; late authorization with short SHOW→correct pixels moves it upstream. If both new modes still show the same visible delay at the same boundary as legacy, report H1 insufficient and return the matching traces. A shorter software marker alone cannot select a winner.

11. SCOPE LOCK / NO-TOUCH

Migrate the existing isolated-eligible standalone lockscreen ORB/orbOnly animated case (including API 35 and existing eligible API 34+ devices), with the existing permitted full and discreet variants. Other SDKs, animation-off configurations, CARD/background, launcher RemoteViews and Flutter dashboard retain their supported rendering and behavior. Retain known legitimate exclusions, ownership, window type, bounds, click/drag behaviors, focusability, settings, palette and offline data. No persistent overlay under keyguard, new system privilege, notification-timeout trick, frame-skipping policy that hides stalls, forced release, global process/thread-priority override, large exported data, or off-screen live animation. No global switch to SurfaceView on unrelated routes, and no deletion of the legacy controls before separately authorized physical acceptance. No new financial settings screen.

12. LAYERS / BOUNDS / OWNERSHIP

Service/Main alone authorizes disclosure and synchronously revokes presentation. One existing bounded accessibility overlay root owns logical visibility, layout, touches and removal. Add exactly one SurfaceView child on the candidate route, default Z below its parent UI but above the window background via the normal SurfaceView hole, with per-pixel translucent holder configured before creation. Use the real ORB resource-derived bounds and centered circle; never setZOrderOnTop or create a second WindowManager window. Test alpha over two known contrasting underlays and verify touch remains with the original root. The old material View with XML ID fluvi_financial_snapshot_orb retains its original typed behavior for CARD/legacy; use GONE/lazy creation per route. Avoid a hidden competing animation, old pool, driver or cold GPU preparer for candidate. Root preparation when detached must create no live Surface, scheduled frame loop or visible window.
One HandlerThread/Looper per active ORB rendering service owner while required; worker owns shader instances, mutable drawing state, phase and its Choreographer. Main owns view/holder callbacks and forwards an immutable target with generation. Keys bind service, capture (for evidence only), wake, show/attach, surface generation, privacy epoch, palette/material digest and actual pixels. One pending frame callback, one newest immutable scene update, one current target, one in-flight holder operation; delayed messages carry their original identity. No app-owned HardwareBuffer slot pool, cross-thread apply, first-vs-steady buffer handoff, SurfaceControl child or pressure switch for the candidate. SurfaceView still uses platform queues, HWUI, RenderThread and GPU; worker-thread API calls do not establish independence from platform scheduling.

14. IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT

A. Service and admission. Keep existing visibility classifier, system snapshot reader, exclusions, actual positive Main admission and privacy checks authoritative. Refactor the queue/dispatch boundary to allow exactly one safe speculative read, never speculative display. Publish an immutable Main-owned snapshot of detached/no-show-in-progress plus authority and freshness revision. Update it before operations that can attach, increase disclosure, revoke or change a relevant preference. Under queueLock, reserve the existing coalesced compatible B only after completed A is HIDDEN_UNKNOWN/NO_MAIN_MARKER with complete roots, no truncation, no stale flags, no contradictory/freshness escalation, detached state and matching generations. The reserved B uses its own event time, ID and current freshness obligations. No carryover markers from A. The reservation is eligible only when the current detached-negative policy with B present selects CONTINUE_PENDING with unchanged visibility epoch. Do not expand eligibility to ROOT_UNAVAILABLE or visible withdrawal.
Enqueue A's ordinary ordered Main apply and release only the one physical reader for B. One preceding ordered apply, one active/reserved read, at most one coalesced latest pending request; never build a queue of completed speculative answers or start C before A settles. Capture the reserved compatible follow-up ID for A's pending/retry decision, rather than losing it when removing B from pending. B may finish early; hold its result for ordered apply. At A apply compare the saved authoritative snapshot; on changed state, invalidate the result and reschedule any necessary fresh inspection under current identity via existing reconciliation. A's completion cannot clear B's reader slot; generations settle exactly once. Never hold queueLock across Android IPC or Main handoff. Current terminal/hide signals always revoke immediately, including while B is reading. An in-flight Binder read may finish after revoke; its result is discarded. Preserve full serial behavior whenever the proof conditions fail. All three candidate APK modes use this same gate. Only the deterministic A/B instrumentation changes this ordering for comparison.

B. Route selection and service integration. Introduce one explicit render selection at the actual eligible window/controller boundary: SURFACE_LIVE default, SURFACE_STATIC diagnostic, LEGACY_R11 diagnostic. Each visible lifetime snapshots configured and effective modes; do not mutate an active target for a console click. On hidden boundary install the newest selection and prepare the correct material before the next wake as possible. Add one three-option control in the existing Debug Console keyguard area. Return configured mode, effective mode and pending-boundary status, preserve across service restart for a comparison, allow restore to default with one tap. Use existing runtime monitoring MethodChannel in lib/core/diagnostics/keyguard_timing_capture_bridge.dart with new get/set handled in MainActivity. The capture commands that dispatch to IO must not mutate a Main-owned window there; serialize the setting and hand off on Main. No setting can grant eligibility or increase privacy. Limit mode overrides to diagnostic builds through a verified build-purpose/debug/profile gate. Default render mode must be visible in the frozen export and real packaged profile. Existing unsupported/API/static/non-target configurations take their existing compatible path. Candidate true/false eligibility is independent of receiving a debug command. Physically testable after normal install, without adb or choosing a hidden experimental toggle.

C. First image and material continuity. In the candidate standalone path replace old detached custom-buffer preparation with one worker-built immutable full-size poster, keyed by actual size/density, render configuration, canonical colors/effect/portal, visual variant, privacy and phase anchor. Before any disclosure always have a preparation path for the approved neutral variant. A prepared full variant may be held only where current settings and the application's data policy permit it; no financial text, screenshots, persistent pixel cache or synthetic expanded permission. Never bind FULL just because it is cached. Prioritize needed neutral+allowed active image; strictly bound to two current variant entries and one in-progress generation, superseded completions discarded; no unbounded bitmap-size or per-frame allocation. Prepare on service connection/settings/material/known target-size change and after legitimate withdrawal where necessary. Cache misses must not block Main, show authorization or teardown. Never animate while detached. Nothing predrawn into a live window while hidden.
Extract the ORB-only drawing primitives from KeyguardHeaderMaterialView, reusing KeyguardHeaderShader.configure(profile,width,height,time), KeyguardMaterialScene.timeAt/anchoredAt, canonical neutralized profile and existing static-gradient behavior. Preserve deep-drift/dual-tide/portal state, real palette, edge, continuity and the existing compatible material transition. Copy mutable profile arrays defensively; construct separate shader/Paint objects per worker usage and capture correct immutable commands for a cached frame. One implementation for drawing an ORB onto a hardware Canvas. Create poster by recording the same commands in an android.graphics.Picture on the worker and materializing Bitmap.createBitmap(picture,width,height,Bitmap.Config.HARDWARE) on eligible APIs; validate RuntimeShader/alpha/pixel identity with the on-device independent control. Do not draw RuntimeShader onto a software bitmap. Cap by the actual supported geometry and avoid per-frame readback. Isolate this offscreen preparation from a live target via its key, cancel obsolete work, and do not schedule it ahead of a currently authorized first frame. A missing/stale prepared image uses the current safe neutral poster if genuinely available and permitted; otherwise stay safely hidden/transparent until a permitted first image is ready. Record the delay, miss reason and first correct positive separately. Repeated missing images are a failed performance outcome. Never certify blank/neutral fallback as first correct requested FULL.
Both new modes post the same prepared image for the same authorized content on the same producer surface. For a given test seed, static holds that image with no animation ticks; live proceeds at the next worker display frame. On first display anchor the running timeline to the phase represented by the poster, not the arbitrary wall time at cold preparation. On real withdrawal freeze the last authorized phase for a compatible reattach; reconstruct a correct current poster for that anchor. Palette/privacy/size changes invalidate incompatible entries. Preserve the legacy semantics for continuously changing compatible profiles and the existing transition duration where applicable. For static mode, update on real allowed content/size changes and required platform redraws only. Correct neutral appearance is a positive visual requirement, including first transition pixels.

D. Draw and lifecycle. Main constructs the eligible SurfaceView and registers SurfaceHolder.Callback2 before attachment; use surfaceCreated/surfaceChanged/actual geometry plus explicit SHOW authorization in either arrival order. Main may install an inert child while the root is being built. Draw only when the current generation is authorized and a usable surface of the correct format/size exists. Use SurfaceHolder.lockHardwareCanvas and unlockCanvasAndPost from exactly one worker. Every frame fully clears transparent pixels and draws the true circle; honor the existing scene and alpha. On success, first and subsequent frames go to the same managed target; keep the queue platform-owned. Drive live motion by the worker Looper's Choreographer and actual frame times, one outstanding callback; coalesce obsolete frame demand. No schedule-ahead loop, Main invalidation pump, unbounded buffers, duplicate clock, or guessed fixed refresh rate. Profile lock/draw/post separately so a framework/driver stall is visible. Never derive future phase by adding a fixed amount per callback. Re-evaluate on surfaceRedrawNeededAsync, acknowledge its completion once after the correct operation or explicit cancellation. Callback completion is an OS lifecycle acknowledgement, not visibility proof.
Worker state: detached/prepared → authorized/waiting for surface → active static or active live → revoked → retired. The holder handle is owned for a single generation and not revived after surfaceDestroyed. Main can revoke immediately without waiting for draw or cleanup to initiate visual hide. Maintain an admission gate for in-flight holder access; worker enters only with the exact current token, leaves in finally, each successful lock is paired with one legal unlock/post even under exception, and no future lock begins after revoke. Prepare shaders, scene updates, diagnostics and other expensive work outside the holder critical interval. On surfaceDestroyed invalidate first; synchronize with completion of any operation that already entered so nobody touches that holder after callback return. Worker must never wait for Main or a main-executor callback during this interval. Do not time out and then access a destroyed surface. Record teardown wait and flag any long driver lock/post under §15. Coalesce callback completion without holding a monitor across an unrelated Main/Worker join. Service dispose removes frame callbacks, cancels queued target work, releases references and safely terminates worker after outstanding access drains. Hidden worker may retain bounded immutable preparation; no recurring callback/slot churn.
Use a distinct target generation and child instance across disclosure reductions. An old generation's late unlock, completion or callback cannot post to, uncover or unhide the replacement child. On a full→discreet downgrade immediately invalidate old permission and hide the old child at the window-owner boundary; show only a pre-approved locally prepared opaque-inside-the-circle discreet guard if necessary while a new target is created. It must preserve the ORB's correct transparent exterior and let no stale full content through the circle. Retire this temporary non-animated guard only after the current target has valid confirmed content and the visual handoff is coherent. Secure by actually withdrawing the old surface; do not rely on a transparent overlay hiding old pixels, on arbitrary sleep, or on treating post as proof of composition. Observe it on the independent compositor, including the first transition frame. If the required atomic visual/privacy contract cannot be demonstrated, record FAIL and return evidence rather than shipping a normal release. No second live renderer or pressure transition. Discreet→full always requires new positive authorization.
On material/driver failure record precise cause, stop recurring work, revoke the affected generation, present only an authorized canonical safe static image at the bounded root when available, otherwise withdraw. Label DEGRADED/UNAVAILABLE; this cannot count as successful SURFACE_LIVE or be silently converted to legacy. Re-attempt on the next genuine lifecycle/material generation only. Keep API/SDK checks at route selection, not inside every frame.

E. Hide. Keep display-off/unlock/exclusion and visible-UNKNOWN policies. For each true withdrawal the first Main operation invalidates authorization and makes the current root/child non-visible/non-interactive using the existing root visibility/window contract; cancel pending show, successor publications and subscriptions for that exact lifetime. Submit actual window removal promptly. Start/schedule resource retirement independently of visual withdrawal; entering platform surfaceDestroyed still obeys D. Do not wait for a render tick, compositor receipt, new tree crawl, timer, GPU preparation or cleanup before issuing local hide/removal. Do not defer required removal or change remove semantics merely to improve the return timestamp. Preserve actual decision, local hide, removal begin/return, and real surface destruction as different observations. Already-detached terminal cleanup is a separate event. Compare first usable event/callback to evidence that the last ORB pixels disappeared. Nothing in this plan promises availability of an earlier Android callback.

F. Debug Console and export. Use the existing dedicated reducer plus KeyguardExportBudget; implement compact per-attempt R12 summaries, versioned and parseable under the current UTF-8 byte budget (≤32 KiB). Give at least first retained cold, later warm/worst samples and all actual retained withdrawal rows priority over repeated verbose per-route UNOBSERVED fields. Preserve existing capture clocks/semantics, original omitted-attempt/critical-record/gap counts and actual omission identities; preserve an external untruncated trace in device suites. Store primitives in bounded rings off the hot path; no per-frame strings, disk writes or cross-thread wait. For OFF disable optional bookkeeping, for LIGHT retain route/outcome/timing, for FULL include the bounded worst examples.
Record service/process/wake/request/show/hide ID, privacy and surface generations, configured/effective route and degrade reason; callback & event time/source availability, inspection read queue/start/end, previous apply queued/entered, read-ahead eligible/reserved/rejected reason, fresh authority read, final SHOW, add, holder create/change/size, poster hit/miss/source/phase identifier (no financial data), worker demand/entry, first valid lock/post, first distinct successor, frame clock, lock/draw/post wall and thread CPU, root traversal marker separately, retire/revoke/remove/destroy and post-revoke rejections. Report first/last sample plus distributions, worst small bounded gap with frame and thread identity. Include true measured display period where supported. Uptime for app event joins, System.nanoTime for short monotonic spans, thread CPU for owned work. For cross-tool traces establish an explicit clock anchor and uncertainty. Distinguish submitted, committed when genuinely observable, target-layer latch/presentation when independently observable, correct composited pixels, and user-observed visual behavior. Missing means UNOBSERVED with reason. Do not relabel lock/post, PixelCopy(surface), screen-off or removeReturn as physical visibility.

G. Mandatory repair to the admission fixture. Patch the SAME instrumentation entry point r12DetachedNegativeCanReadOneSuccessorBeforeOrderedApply in the real-service test, keeping its stock-compatible observation implementation in androidTest. Implement the following order. All changes to set-up stimulus and observation are test-only. Keep the shipping source byte-identical to stock for the baseline. Candidate-only production diagnostic events can supplement, never substitute for the common A/B oracle.

G1. Run UUID and clean start. Instrumentation owns a unique output subdirectory and records run UUID, PID/process instance, capture ID, mode, app and harness SHA. Start on a clean disposable API35 emulator with the existing insecure test lock only, real service, FULL capture and real display. Install the probe and an authentic pass-through system reader before driving the measured wake. The override delegates exactly once to AndroidKeyguardSystemStateReader for each purpose and returns that identical result. Only record actual values. Clean up the previous overrides, service/preferences, keyguard state, background samplers and density in finally, including failed initialization and held latches. Resolve registered layout and signer as specified elsewhere.

G2. Prepare eligibility without depending on the first SystemUI window. Establish the real display interactive+ON, primary display, user-unlocked-since-boot and keyguard currently locked, with the overlay detached/awaiting. Use an instrumented set-up barrier while waking: for each genuine MAIN_KEYGUARD candidate in the setup phase only, mask only the registry's affirmative MAIN ids in its eligible SystemUI windows to keep the service detached. Leave real credential/shade/foreign windows, display, package, layer and other IDs untouched. Use KeyguardSurfaceClassifier's exact stock marker set in the test (reflect the immutable set in a pinned baseline if necessary), never a copy of a partial classifier. Record that masking is a synthetic NEGATIVE stimulus, and require an actual complete unmasked positive control separately. Unavailable roots, truncation, a foreign occluder and terminal system signals cannot be upgraded to a valid target. A test-only wrapper may collect a bounded list of rejection tuples; no permission is ever injected. Use the real pass-through samples and actual marked test callbacks to identify stable setup; if already attached, fail setup explicitly or start the planned clean process, never count a hide as evidence that it had been detached earlier.
Keep setup masking active through ordinary untagged requests until the nominated A has reached the measurement boundary. Prevent an opportunistic positive from attaching the real window between the ready signal and capture of A. Switch off masking for the designated B so its tree and result are genuine.

G3. Once prepared, use existing service scheduling on Main to submit one explicitly tagged A (FRAMEWORK_EVENT, current authority), and use a once-only arm to recognize that actual request. Only when A's real tree has the qualifying main marker, a compatible current detached authority, and the masked copy classifies to the candidate negative, schedule one explicitly tagged B through existing scheduleEvaluation BEFORE A's acquisition completes. Verify returned queue identity under queueLock, matching service/wake/visibility/interaction/attach generation and no outstanding required freshness escalation. Record actual pending/replacement/current identities and freshness; retain B's identity before returning from A's snapshots hook. B cannot be introduced for the first time inside A.beforeApply because that would miss the candidate's reservation opportunity. No mock B read, artificial positive, concurrent second tree walk, blind sleep, deadline extension, repeated wake-until-green or setting-wide disable of real incoming events. A superseded tag or drift after original measurement gets a specific, recorded invalid verdict.
Use the existing started(request) and Worker-local scoped inspection identity to associate INSPECTION-purpose pass-through reads with that exact request. Separate pre-tree sample from post-tree sample; single-sample early exit cannot qualify. Record available, primaryDisplay, interactive, displayOn, displayOff, keyguardLocked, userUnlocked, actual uptime and returned decision. Do not infer final state from a later PowerManager read. The synthetic mask only removes *positive MAIN identifiers*; B receives untouched snapshots. A real candidate B can start before A.beforeApply: the observer must handle both event orders.

G4. At A.beforeApply capture the ACTUAL decision and all request identities before any assertion. Validate detached condition and exact current A/B generations. Capture B's reservation/active/pending or its already-recorded read+pending-ordered-apply identity if it finished on the new path. The queue's most recent unrelated replacement is insufficient evidence of B. Hold A's ordered Main apply with the existing bounded latch only for the confirmed negative case, allowing release from an instrumentation test thread independent of Main; no runOnMainSync from B during that hold. Each failed precondition emits expected/actual values, an explicit cause and releases every latch. No PASS by skipping unqualified samples. The temporary screen setup may use a bounded existing prerequisite window; the measured specimen is exactly one tagged pair per scheduled process.
Record A decision on entering its hook, A release signal and actual exit, B original offer, B actual reader entry, B genuine snapshots/reader completion and B ordered Main application, with request IDs, Main/worker thread IDs, monotonic times and an append-order counter to resolve equal ticks. Write the trace after release outside measured/blocked Main; retain failed fixture observations in finally. B may already have started at A hook entry. Stock R11 must exhibit A held with no B start, then real B start only after releasing A. Candidate must exhibit real B acquisition before A release, A's ordered apply before B's apply, no increased disclosure before legitimate fresh authority and at most one actual tree reader. Verify no stale B permission on revoke; keep a separate unit/controlled case where B finishes while A is held. Allow both finite orderings of actual B finish where the production contract permits them; do not require a full Binder read within an artificially tight synchronization window.

G5. After releasing A and observing actual completion, collect the unformatted R11 INSPECTION_FINISHED event keyed by process+capture+session/wake+request ID, stage and original authority. That event's reason is Inspection.surfaceReason; fields include surfaceClassification, rootUnavailable, walkTruncated and abortedStale. For exact stock use a test-only reader of KeyguardCardDiagnostics.reduction.read, then captureLock and the current original TimingCapture.events (or its frozen copy) to copy only this bounded, immutable row after production traceInspectionResult has enqueued it. No waiting inside captureLock, no reading a live ring on a foreign thread, no reflection that mutates production, and no exposing this inspector in release. In R11 traceInspectionResult is queued after A's Main apply; do not wait for this final evidence while A remains held. Bound the observation using the existing test deadline and capture generation. If the row is evicted or not yet observable by the deadline, record EVIDENCE_MISSING; a later attempt's NO_MAIN_MARKER cannot fill it. Record the actual per-request system samples and observed decision even in an early invalid case, before cleanup stops the capture. A final accepted specimen requires all of: A.decision=HIDDEN_UNKNOWN AND A.reason=NO_MAIN_MARKER, complete/nonstale tree, actual system/authority and detach predicates at their specified boundaries, exact compatible B, fresh source identity, healthy cleanup and measured order. A provisional latch signal can never be the verdict.

G6. Host and workflow. Preserve the R11-specific negative comparator in a distinct r12_admission_baseline dispatch. Pin a stock R11 worktree/build with production sources, dependencies, Android build configs, native modules, assets and app debug sources at 1d196247. Overlay only the audited androidTest test files/helpers or compile a separate compatible test APK; the harness/workflow runs from its own immutable tag. Include an explicit path allowlist and source diff, full SHA and hashes of both APKs, test method, process and run UUID. Keep the shared fixture test stock-compilable; isolate tests requiring new candidate types in other files. Restore r12_contract as the R12 candidate product suite and register the three fixed mode choices described in §17. For baseline builds avoid default-branch workflow input incompatibility: use the proven dispatch workflow/tag route and its declared choices, verify the chosen SHA and scope in the archive. The legacy renderer on new service scheduling is a runtime render control only; it is not the stock old-queue baseline.
Change the shell/Python verdict to parse typed, operation-correlated rows. Validate runner completion/exit (adb may exit 0 for an AndroidJUnit failure), app/test APK hash and installed identity, confirmed test execution without a transport timeout, extraction statuses, single intended method, exactly the expected assertion with genuine order observation for stock, or a genuine green method for candidate, cleanup PASS for the same run, no secondary/suppressed exceptions, and real nonempty artifacts. Ignore no failed untar/probe/identity checks. Host controls must fail on stale output after force-stop and on a valid unrelated NO_MAIN_MARKER event. Make assertions about the actual capture/edited ZIP and inputs, rather than checking whether an expected sentence exists in arbitrary stdout. Preserve the counterexample package on any failure.

G7. Execution independence. After cheap host tests and compile, dispatch at most one corrected stock baseline for this specific fixture revision. Implement and exercise SurfaceView presentation/diagnostics in parallel as independent work. Run one candidate admission/control suite on the actual candidate revision plus the mode runs in §17. If the same boundary still cannot be reached, return the recorded A/B tuple rather than another identical expensive run. An outstanding baseline/result remains open in the report/full-release gates. It cannot justify another fixture-only handback, omission of the product repair, or publication of stock R11 as the evaluation APK.

15. PERFORMANCE GATE

Use the second R11 capture as a repeatability control, not as the result of a patch. Pair endpoint with endpoint; report first-cycle SCREEN_ON→correct image separately from a warm wake callback→submit. The direct handoff has already occurred in 3 ms on this phone when prerequisites were ready. Do not tune this clock to declare success. Record correlations and uncertainty for qualified screen pixels across wake, the stable 5 s lock interval and unlock. Successful fixture selection and ordering are mechanism checks, never phone acceptance.

For each mode report fresh-process first wake and each warm cycle individually, aggregate only equivalent cases. Record display refresh, process, API, geometry, palette/effect, exact source/hash, prewarm hit/miss, route, capture mode and interval class. Compare renderer modes with identical admission/scene/window/fixture. Separate (a) signal→positive SHOW, (b) SHOW→first correct composed ORB, (c) first→next genuinely distinct composed frame, (d) sustained locked cadence, and (e) actual event→callback→local hide→last externally visible ORB. Report event→remove return independently. Measure diagnostics overhead by comparing a matched LIGHT/OFF timing-only control to FULL; do not infer observer cost from cumulative consumer-lock duration.
Engineering acceptance budgets chosen for R12, not promises about handset physics: in a five-second continuously authorized, non-transition locked interval at the measured refresh, candidate frame submissions p95 inter-frame gap ≤2 display periods and zero unexplained candidate-owned gaps >50 ms. Report worst and counts over 2 periods/50/80 ms, plus externally measured cadence where coverage qualifies. SURFACE_STATIC should make no periodic submissions after its required first/redraw. For actual withdraw, target decision→local hide ≤1 display period on every measured repeat; report event-delivery and compositor portions regardless. For first correct positive pixels and first distinct successor, pair by environment/process state; report absolute bracket widths for new and legacy. A candidate is faster on a paired endpoint only where observation uncertainty supports the direction. Show mode-by-mode first-correct, last-visible and steady-motion results. If a late event/cold sample worsens, show it. Mechanism PASS alone cannot meet the product goal. No averaged-away cold start or fabricated p95 from four wakes.
Hold shared services/refresh equal. Separate automated stable 5 s locked and unlocked transition windows. Short screen recordings/sampling can disturb rendering; run timing-only and visual processes separately. Sample presentation timestamps or trustworthy compositor FrameTimeline entries for the matching layer, with layer mapping and observed data-source support; otherwise label absent. A static duplicate is not a newly animated frame. A real-queue cadence or cycle metric alone does not measure what the user saw. R12 remains open until the owner tests the exact APK.

16. IMPLEMENTATION ORDER

Execution amendment: implement and locally test the repaired stock fixture/oracle first, then run that one device check independently of the production presenter implementation. Do not idle waiting for a stock CI verdict before beginning the planned runtime work. Deliver the integrated candidate and actual-source CI results. A fixture-only result is an intermediate checkpoint.

Pin branch/app, preserve baseline/harness and protected behavior. Create RED fixtures, calibrated positive/negative image controls and executable mode selection contract. Implement the admission scheduling change and tests as a separately identifiable change. Introduce the candidate presenter/worker and shared canonical-material preparation; bind real service window, current privacy and destruction before enabling candidate default on eligible ORB. Wire the three diagnostics modes and compact ownership evidence; port the full service entry and retain explicit legacy-mode tests. Validate cheap gates first. Run each fixed scoped device suite and capture all independent evidence, then eligible full gates and normal delivery. Build the exact-source Human APK and publish evidence even when independently possible after a failed gate. Never substitute another branch, older APK, a standalone test Activity or a screenshot-only prototype for the candidate.

17. VALIDATION

In addition to the listed cheap commands, run bash -n scripts/test-keyguard-r12-admission-baseline.sh and the expanded python3 scripts/test-keyguard-r12-harness.py on the actual baseline harness and candidate host revision. Require all negative controls in §13. Keep the structured exact-pair extracts, raw fixture, logcat, untouched failed ZIP, JUnit result, mode, screenshots/trace as applicable, and checksums. Stock outcome: valid RED_EXPECTED=actual_service_serial_order. Candidate: correct eligible read-ahead plus ordered safe application with a passing test. If a prerequisites/identity/evidence check fails, both suites must fail closed. Local compile or fake-adb results cannot replace these API35 observations.

Run from a clean checkout on the established build VM (Flutter 3.41.4 / Dart 3.11.1, Android SDK 35, Java 17); use the authenticated GitHub Actions API35 x86_64 KVM device backend, recorded previous geometry 1080×2400 at 420 dpi. Check actual versions and geometry. The VM does not need a local emulator. Add the named R12 harness/tests before the new commands are run. Retain old scripts and workflow choices. Cheap and compile gates:
    git diff --check
    bash scripts/verify-fluvi-boundaries.sh
    bash scripts/test-keyguard-lower-environment.sh
    python3 scripts/test-keyguard-r09-panel-harness.py
    python3 scripts/test-keyguard-r10-cold-harness.py
    python3 scripts/test-keyguard-r11-cold-harness.py
    python3 scripts/test-keyguard-r12-harness.py
    flutter test test/core/diagnostics/keyguard_timing_capture_bridge_test.dart test/core/debug/keyguard_timing_capture_console_test.dart test/boundary/keyguard_first_render_architecture_boundary_test.dart --reporter expanded
    flutter test test/boundary/dashboard_interaction_performance_boundary_test.dart test/boundary/human_diagnostic_apk_delivery_boundary_test.dart test/boundary/dashboard_avatar_profile_boundary_test.dart --reporter expanded
    (cd android && ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest :fluvi-core:testDebugUnitTest :app:testDebugUnitTest --no-daemon --max-workers=3 --console=plain)
    flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos
    bash scripts/test-fluvi-fast.sh --reporter expanded
Expected: source-clean build output, real targeted RED/green on same behavior, correct test discovery, no silent skips, no compatibility changes outside scope. Record any prior warning/failure separately and retain exact results for the final source after any change.

Candidate diagnostic choices in .github/workflows/fluvi-core.yml: register r12_legacy, r12_static, r12_live and convert the existing r12_contract to a candidate suite after splitting out r12_admission_baseline. Add allowlisted shell selector and Python host tests enforcing source/app-test APK identity, requested mode, entry class/method, process freshness, geometry, JUnit executed count, expected capture and mandatory artifact upload even on failure. Reuse known working emulator bootstrap/toolchain. Split modes into independent jobs/dispatches to fit existing limits. Do not rerun R11's six failures with the route accidentally defaulting to new: select LEGACY_R11 explicitly and record real old slot states. Full gate retains the strict isolated regression suite and adds a separate production-entry suite actually exercising SURFACE_LIVE. An unresolved legacy failure stays in report/gate according to its existing contract. New candidate behavior uses surface generation and true presented identity, never placeholder slot/fence values.

Device experiment, pre-bounded: per each of three modes, one fresh timing process and one separate fresh calibrated visual process, each with the first service attach and three warm wake/unlock cycles in consistent settings. Include a stable locked five-second window before unlock in at least one warm cycle of each process. Fixed duration windows and independent process setup, not a sleep-based readiness oracle. A short matched LIGHT/OFF timing control for candidate uses two additional fresh processes maximum (one for each capture setting); other controls run once per fixed case. One contract panel for ordered real admission/lifetime/visual cases and legacy regression checks. Preserve results from every scheduled phase, including failed cases. The existing full native 2×30 service gate is separate and remains mandatory before ordinary delivery. Do not trigger repeated identical full workflows after failure.
For A/C/B/A distinct producer controls use the repository's calibrated A=1.196795, C=1.5234617, B=3.75 or the pinned fixture's exact float representations, same palette and orientation. Test the target's real composite via screen-level acquisition and independent controls; PixelCopy on the component's own Surface is a useful producer check only. Keep the existing meaningful-difference and equality controls in compareOrbPixels and check the alpha boundary including corners over real contrasting underlays. Positive target includes the one expected ORB variant; add wrong-palette/phase and no-ORB negatives. A single magenta fiducial in the wrong app/layer cannot stand for ORB correctness.
Calibrate geometry and independent underlay/fiducial on this emulator configuration before the fresh test process. Keep calibration outside that process, preserve geometry, rotation, display and background identity, take a known empty reference. During transition collect bounded screen-composited ROI or a short external compositor sequence with monotonic pre/post brackets and stable geometry. Keep fixed ROI observable before the ORB gains a window ID; qualify such an early negative only where this independent calibration is valid. No speculative cropping around pixels selected after observing the ORB. Target missing with ambiguous geometry/window/occlusion, screen capture forbidden, white unknown background or missing fiducial → UNKNOWN. A verified white crop where the positive ORB should be visible is a failure. Never change security flags to get pixels. Save first sample, last valid negative, first valid positive, first distinct successor, last positive and first confirmed absence; report unbounded intervals when required endpoints are missing. Keep native captures and the small failed ROI artifacts; avoid testing handset timing from encoded video frame counts without clock/uncertainty. Separate sampler from timing runs, no formatting/disk writes in timing scopes. Record availability and capture cadence. Use actual keyguard-permitted state and current credential/occluder observations; display-off, keyguard-locked, app-withdrawn, global idle and visible compositor absence are separate predicates.
If the contract/scope condition fails, preserve original sources and evidence, classify app/test/fixture/oracle/infra, report every independent failure together. Correct clear mechanical fixture errors within the contract and revalidate the new source; return any new design/privacy decision to reviewer. After all required scoped entry conditions pass, run full native then ordinary CI. Continue graph, report and clearly marked evaluation APK independently if full delivery is blocked.

18. COMMIT DISCIPLINE

Keep admission, production renderer/window integration, diagnostics/test harness and tooling/report changes attributable. Record prerequisite/diff, old and new ownership, lifecycle and regression risks, RED and validation on the actual SHA. Avoid full CI for intermediate checkpoints. Check graphs, reports, workflow and must-pass conditions on the immutable candidate. Append to docs/FLUVI_ENGINEERING_JOURNAL.md with each substantive source SHA, exact run IDs, artifact links and verdicts. Preserve concurrent entries. If the final app/fixture changes after testing, report which exact gates were rerun on it; do not attach previous results as final PASS. Place graph and documentation on known separate tooling/docs commits, never modify the APK's source attribution.

19. PUSH / BUILD / GRAPH REGENERATION

Stage this ONE immutable negative-control dispatch from the stock-compatible harness tag. Set harness_ref to the actual pushed tag, verify it resolves to the documented harness SHA, and run:
    gh workflow run fluvi-core.yml -R elizerpist/exptv2 --ref "$harness_ref" -f native_diagnostic=true -f native_scope=r12_admission_baseline
The product APK and all four candidate scopes below must target the NEW production SHA. Do not tag the same harness commit as a repaired production candidate. If an independently blocked permission prevents hosting, still build, sign, hash and test what is reachable, record the failed route and use the established verified alternative.

Use a clean pinned worktree on the established authenticated VM. Set candidate_sha from the final checked app/fixture source. Create a unique immutable tag (no retag), push branch without forcing, and verify the remote ref. Configure the new scope mappings in §17 before invoking them. Check the workflow definition on the default branch can accept the dispatch and the tag runs the intended version. Record actual headSha, scope, job names and results. Example commands (bash variables refer to the actual verified values for this run):
    candidate_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

8. CURRENT SOURCE FACTS

FluviFinancialCardPresenter.full(content, showEvent) calls content.orbBitmap() before returning. Its three other producers use the neutral content's orbBitmap(). The helper allocates a new ARGB_8888 96×96 bitmap and paints the gradient circle. Each allocation has 36,864 bytes of pixel payload before other objects. showFullContent builds full(cached, showEvent) on repeated eligible inspections even when KeyguardCardWindow.showOrUpdate later returns NO_OP. The new bitmap is then unused. No runtime counter in either phone export measures this work. On a Surface attach, selectRenderRoute sets the legacy orb GONE; apply(force=true) still dereferences presentation.orb and binds it. The Surface presenter draws from the current profile/poster through its own worker. On the legacy path there are two legitimate consumers of the same per-presentation bitmap. For a real launcher RemoteViews the getter must produce nonnull pixels. The notification's content.orbBitmap() is a separate direct caller. Do not conflate any of these with the 168×168 animated Surface output.

8. CURRENT SOURCE FACTS

K/FluviKeyguardCardService.kt copies event type, window/display, package, changes and event uptime at onAccessibilityEvent. The generic scheduleEvaluation request does not carry all of this origin. INSPECT is also reachable for an ambiguous own-window event. K/KeyguardCardInspectionQueue.kt has an active reader, one coalesced pending slot and a separate preceding/reserved relationship. A reserved predecessor or in-flight reader is not an unstarted pending event.

After worker read and Main handoff, applyInspection gates by service, wake, interaction, visibility and attach generations. Real admission/disclosure also samples current system state. A successful decision updates appliedDecision and can immediately show cached/loading/unavailable/discreet content or later publish resolved full content. applyResolvedPresentation calls overlay.showOrUpdate. On ATTACHED it sets overlayAttachGeneration, publishes new authority and invokes preservePendingReconciliation("attach", requirePending=true). That function can issue a fresh synthetic authorityReconcile:attach request with a new callback time. offer replaces the old pending slot. Stock does not carry a causal parent in that path. Thus a subsequent negative on the new generation is not by itself the result of the prior external request. A further, genuinely new external event can also replace the synthetic request.

By contrast, after recoverable visible UNKNOWN/OCCLUDED, handleRecoverableSurface calls hideImmediately(...terminalWake=false), records a contradictory-read freshness obligation and may reacquire the compatible pending intent with a new ID under current authority while retaining its original callback time. Preserve this distinction. Terminally unlocked/display-off states already have a separate exclusion path. KeyguardCardWindow owns current attachment and effective route. The Surface worker owns generation-qualified posting. KeyguardCardSettings.kt owns the bounded capture reducer/export.

9. PROVEN / UNPROVEN / MISSING

PROVEN: two same-wake second attachments and subsequent actual withdrawals; the two known hide callbacks arrived after their respective presentation scopes; missing critical show rows; stock can replace a pending request at attach; zero eager paints in the 51 measured presentation scopes. In two slow first withdrawals the inspection consumed 130/174 ms and local hide followed the decision by 1 ms.

UNPROVEN: a suitable earlier independent SystemUI event existed in either wake; the second attachment was unnecessary at that instant; the user saw the corresponding generation. A genuine temporary MAIN return, a post-attach transition, and a poster/Surface transition remain plausible. Slow first show or first withdrawal has a separate measured path.

MISSING EVIDENCE: immutable origin/pending identity before publication, stock replacement chain and its actual outcome, and independent composition covering the transitions. All missing endpoints are UNOBSERVED. The R13 phone report is partial improvement, still open.

10. ROOT-CAUSE OR FORENSIC GATE

Selected contract and stock RED. Establish an actual recoverable withdrawal in the production service, detached state and existing A read of complete MAIN. While A is in its read-to-apply interval, deliver B as a distinct, positively attributable external primary-display SystemUI window event through the production ingress/queue. Independently control an excluding surface after A sampled MAIN and before A publishes. Observe B physically pending at the pre-publication snapshot. Exercise the real stock add, attach-generation advance, pending replacement by synthetic reconciliation if it happens, and the actual later current read/withdrawal. Label B, the replacement R and any later C separately. A stock excess add under independently known exclusion and its absence on the candidate is the decisive application-level test. A false inference that B itself ran is a fixture error.

Paired controls: same ordering with B confirming genuine fresh MAIN must return exactly once in this wake. With no qualifying pending B and only a later post-attach C, both versions must admit A immediately and withdraw normally on C. On the 1+3 natural cycles keep all observations, including zero occurrences. Natural incidence measures external relevance; absence in four cycles does not veto a reachable deterministic production-service RED. A mock that calls policy directly or manufactures an impossible queue sequence cannot establish the RED. If valid production ingress, actual attach/replacement or independent ordering cannot be demonstrated in the specified control, classify fixture/instrumentation or contract failure with raw evidence and return that part to the reviewer. No speculative release.

Protect real recovery after a temporary occluder. Bypass this new rule on route/configuration/selection changes, static/legacy/CARD and unsupported configurations. Never retain old FULL pixels while undecided. No global cooldown, delay-until-next-wake, arbitrary extra scan, read of a previous wake as authority, or event-to-hide shortcut. 14. IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT

Implement in this order.

A. Observation and identity. Main assigns a monotonic per-session event identity at ingress, using only scalar non-sensitive metadata copied while Android owns the event. Distinguish external SystemUI, own, ambiguous, synthetic retry/reconcile and same-intent reacquisition. Preserve the original external ID through reacquisition and record a separate request ID each time. A synthetic attach-reconcile optionally reports the displaced request and origin as diagnostic ancestry; it never inherits positive external authorization. On offer use the actual pending slot immediately before/after replacement under queueLock. Do not join by time or nearest generation. Preserve scheduleEvaluation(String, Long?, Long?, KeyguardWindowFreshness, KeyguardCardInspectionRequest?) as the actual five-argument JVM entry by forwarding to a distinctly named common implementation. The existing reflection-based ordered-read-ahead fixture looks it up by signature.

B. Main owns at most one small recovery record per actual eligible visible withdrawal. Capture effective live route, privacy/selection and authority at the original attached owner; install the record only after actual local withdrawal/detached outcome, using the resulting current authority. Do not arm on failed removal, pre-show hidden UNKNOWN or terminal cleanup. Clear on real successful replacement attach, terminal signal, new wake/session, cancellation or changed eligibility/privacy/selection. Hidden negatives during the same recovery do not renew the one-use allowance. Hold no View, Surface, bitmap, accessibility object or renderer lease in this record.

C. In applyInspection keep normal rejection, freshness and ADMISSION read gates. Before assigning appliedDecision, resetting retry state or entering any presentation/financial path, check this exact predicate: detached current WITHDRAWN_AWAITING_SURFACE, matching unused recovery, current complete MAIN result allowing the current privacy level, same effective-eligible animated standalone LIVE configuration, and a qualifying pending B. Sample only inspectionQueue.pendingRequest() under queueLock. B must be unstarted, same full current authority, distinct external framework SystemUI window event on the primary display, positively identified as external. Require valid original event uptime (0 < event <= callback), event >= A.readStart, callback strictly after A.readStart and received before the Main decision snapshot. Use established ingress order to distinguish timestamp ties at the publication boundary; ambiguous read-start/order ties take ordinary behavior. Exclude previous-wake or cloned old events, own or ambiguous events, synthetic reconciles/timers, reserved predecessors and already-active reads. Use the existing effective-route eligibility rule outside queueLock. On unsupported, stale, unproven or changed origin/configuration take the ordinary policy path, including existing hard exclusions.

D. On first match atomically consume the one-use allowance on Main, record DEFERRED and return before appliedDecision/show/add/content mutation. Do not enqueue a scan, retry, timer, redraw or any new worker. Existing completion finally blocks release A; the existing pending item or its genuinely coalesced replacement runs. Revalidate all normal gates on that result. A negative stays withdrawn, a fresh complete positive can restore exactly once even under a flood, and a terminal event invalidates the record immediately. Preserve normal bounded reconciliation on stale results and ack required cache clears only when the physical read establishes the boundary. Keep positive decision, actually applied result, deferred, stale, rejected, and failed WindowManager add distinct in diagnostics. Existing financial resolve returns still check session/epoch/focus/full state and fresh PUBLICATION before producing content.

E. On capture, preserve compact identity-linked records for previous real hide, A read/apply, pre-publication pending B, any exact B→R→C replacement(s) or omission counter, actual outcome, later withdrawal and independent frame availability. Use capture/session/wake/recovery/authority/request/origin/show/hide/attach generation and comparable uptime units; note System.nanoTime/thread CPU separately for cost. Cover a hold without allocating a fictitious show ID. Log event receipt and system state only to the degree observed. Budget fixed records per retained recovery, reserve compact rows and footer first, expose saturation/omission counts, and format on the existing diagnostic worker/export path. Keep OFF free of capture work. No synchronous I/O, per-frame strings or old FULL pixels while undecided.

15. PERFORMANCE GATE

First show and already-visible updates gain zero reader calls and zero mandatory waits from R14. Zero incremental physical reads on the qualifying path. Per-wake targets: remove a verified unnecessary add + subsequent real removal from the qualifying sequence; stable recovery must still reach a correct current image with at most one additional pre-existing observation before publication. Compare its latency and report the cost even if churn improves. Preserve zero eager bitmap paints/binds in the measured eligible scopes. Report per-episode SCREEN_ON to decision, first producer post/distinct and first observed correct composite; callback -> worker start -> inspection end -> main entry -> decision -> local hide -> remove return. Distinguish first show, re-show and cleanup. Report worst/p95 producer gaps for the available intervals and the actual screen sampling resolution. Do not call a better post rate a physical fix. A persistent slow first withdrawal or initial admission is a separate reviewer decision. Use stock and candidate per-case counts including stale/reconciliation work. The required fresh admission/publication read on a legitimate recovery remains. Count actual root/inspection acquisitions, separately from those system-state reads. A later correct visual recovery and its extra latency must be reported even when an add was saved.

16. IMPLEMENTATION ORDER

Pin the stock runtime and graph. Build the typed observation, controlled-service fixture and host oracle with stock behavior; preserve the stock RED, the late-only control and pressure specimen. Verify the fixture actually reached the tested state and exercised the real attach/replacement. Land the one-use admission change with diagnostics and run the identical controlled cases on candidate. Run cheap compile/tests before spending the hosted native budget. Collect the natural 1+3 block once per comparison, conservatively label sample coverage, and separately run real composition/privacy. Complete the exact-source delivery checks below. A demonstrated contract contradiction goes back to reviewer with evidence; retain and finish all independent work. No guessing, retry-until-green, dropping samples, increasing waits to mask failures or relaxing required gates.

## 2026-11-20 — R14 handset acceptance failed for latency; R15 first-admission decision

The user tested R14 profile build b6c71cfc350819e9a10a33e3e4cb6e078a4198d9 on Nothing A142/API 35 and reported *worse visible render and disappearance lag*. Capture 6fdafefb-36de-4b73-b03f-fbcdc634be0f, LIGHT, process 17215-ecd05baf. Four retained wakes each had one actual add and one actual remove. Their exported recovery histories end at terminal cleanup without a deferred readmission. The controlled R14 readmission repair remains implemented. This physical test did not establish a perceptible improvement and the user has not accepted it.

| Retained attempt | R13 SCREEN_ON → first distinct post | R14 SCREEN_ON → show decision / first post / first distinct post | R14 first read and result | R14 withdrawal event → callback / callback → local hide / local hide → remove return |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| 1 | 278 ms | 112 / 217 / 254 ms | 175 ms, MAIN | 1 / 26 / 64 ms |
| 6 | 146 ms | 198 / 244 / 251 ms | 148 ms, NO_MAIN_MARKER | 74 / 31 / 25 ms |
| 7 | 185 ms | 212 / 253 / 265 ms | 156 ms, ROOT_UNAVAILABLE | 81 / 34 / 27 ms |
| 8 | 238 ms | 173 / 225 / 233 ms | 135 ms, ROOT_UNAVAILABLE | 77 / 12 / 14 ms |

R13 and R14 are different processes and runs; retained attempt numbers identify rows within each run. Attempts 6 and 7 took 105 and 80 ms longer to reach a changed producer frame. Attempts 1 and 8 took 24 and 5 ms less. The latest three warm attempts spent 138/101/130 ms in the *first* active-root call. The phone's warm time from show decision to first producer post was 46/41/52 ms. On withdrawal, all four actual causes were NO_MAIN_MARKER; decision to local invisibility was 1/1/2/1 ms. Neither event time nor a Canvas completion timestamps the display. No second attach in these four samples explains the reported perceptual decline.

The next product experiment targets the whole first inspection on a locked wake. It cannot claim time saved merely by moving an IPC wait from the root to a child. Withdrawal receives event-to-pixel measurement in the same build; a separate timing or privacy issue discovered there returns to the reviewer. R14 automatic validation remains FAIL_INCOMPLETE. The R14 HUMAN_DIAGNOSTIC artifact was REVIEW ONLY. Physical result on this R14 is TESTED / LATENCY NOT ACCEPTED. R15 implementation, validation and delivery are open.

8. CURRENT SOURCE FACTS

The reader obtains the current primary-display window inventory, establishes eligibility for a cache-enabled, unambiguous active window after the applicable freshness boundary, calls getRootInActiveWindow(HYBRID | UNINTERRUPTIBLE), and verifies returned window ID and package availability against the inventory. In the accepted path visibleIds requests existing children using the same batched flags. Other window roots use window.root. Non-visible subtrees are already skipped in the local traversal; up-front platform descendant prefetch can still do work before that traversal chooses its branches. Cache hits, actual platform work and IPC service latency are variable. Android permits the strategy 0 on the API-33+ active-root overload. The candidate preserves the existing per-window route, accepted-root verification and complete local traversal, including the 96-node bound and existing exclusions/failure handling. API references: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/accessibilityservice/AccessibilityService#getRootInActiveWindow(int) and https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/accessibility/AccessibilityNodeInfo#getChild(int,int).

No secure flag exemptions. Inspect ffprobe -show_streams/-show_frames, use presentation order and passthrough frame extraction, no resampling or duplicate-based frame rate estimates. Check disk contour, interior color/pattern and exterior reference with codec tolerance. Include wrong ROI/wallpaper and static false-motion controls. Use independently recognizable system pixels outside the service ROI plus corroborating system state for lockscreen, shade, credential and unlock. 15. PERFORMANCE GATE

One identical app/test APK pair on the same booted API35 AVD, fixed image, configuration, recording pipeline and fixture. Two reverse-order blocks: stock then candidate, candidate then stock. Four fresh service processes, each process-cold first wake plus three warm wakes, 16 total. Archive every slot with system/capture state before its first read. Pre-pair by block, position, route, first-call eligibility, completeness/first classification and comparable tree shape. Record exclusions and unmatched slots; no replacements. Compare real total read including children, outcome/fallback/next inspection, wake/SCREEN_ON to decision, distinct producer and independently identified first correct composite. For a left/right onset bracket report both endpoints and delta range [candidate lower − stock upper, candidate upper − stock lower]. Compare warm paired medians and full range separately per block, plus cold and all-slot end-to-end results. For the primary comparison use wake-to-first-correct bounds aggregated over predeclared matched warm slots; report all endpoints and eligible counts in both blocks. Onsets must improve beyond measured uncertainty in both blocks, with reproducible total-read benefit, no offsetting downstream, classification/privacy or material regression. Changed or absent opportunities cannot establish gain. A separate stable real-service comparison may explain call-cost transfer but cannot replace the natural comparison or turn missing eligible pairs into a pass. No extra retries or synthetic waits inside natural measurements. If intervals overlap, pairs are absent or signs reverse, report NOT ESTABLISHED/adverse as observed. Keep the experiment and diagnostic corrections identifiable.

For W-HIDE provide independently observed start of restricted/unlock scene, last forbidden/first safe bracket, positives before/after and gaps. Record event→callback→queue→read start/end→Main entry→decision→local hide/revoke→remove begin/return; bind holder and last successful post/latch only with matching identity. Record p95/worst producer gaps, video gaps and observer overhead separately. Never sum overlapping scopes. Use “unsampled”, “right/left censored” or “class ambiguous” with bounds, never infer subframe timing. Do not claim zero forbidden pixels between samples.

8. CURRENT SOURCE FACTS AND PLATFORM CONTRACT

The Surface presenter creates one translucent SurfaceView and worker target. The worker locks that system holder, draws the existing poster or live painter, posts and then validates target identity for reporting. revoke blocks new entries. surfaceDestroyed drains an already entered operation. KeyguardCardWindow.hide revokes with hideChild=false, sets root INVISIBLE then calls removeViewImmediate. On FULL→discreet the presenter revokes G1, may change old child visibility, installs the permitted neutral guard, removes the old SurfaceView and authorizes G2. There is no direct hide transaction for already composed R12 LIVE pixels on these paths. In contrast the isolated legacy implementation already submits visibility on an app-owned child. Both a retained buffer and a later in-flight post are possible. Changing only the contents of the last post cannot retire a previously visible image.

Android API35 permits Surface(SurfaceControl), hardware Canvas lock/post on that Surface, an app-created RGBA buffer layer under the SurfaceView control, and Transaction.setVisibility on an app-owned child. SurfaceView.getSurfaceControl is only a parenting handle; never mutate, hide, release or reparent the framework's control itself. The public API and Android 15 SurfaceView buffer-sync implementation are the platform contracts for this plan. [Surface](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/Surface) · [SurfaceView](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/SurfaceView#getSurfaceControl()) · [Builder](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/SurfaceControl.Builder) · [Transaction](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/SurfaceControl.Transaction) · [Android 15 SurfaceView source](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/tags/android-15.0.0_r1/core/java/android/view/SurfaceView.java)

14. IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT

A. Add a small generation-owned output in K/material beside the existing presenter/worker. Main alone owns the borrowed parent binding, child control, visibility submissions and retirement identity. At actual valid host creation/size create a fresh SurfaceControl.Builder().setName(bounded non-sensitive generation identifier).setParent(host.surfaceControl).setBufferSize(width,height).setFormat(PixelFormat.RGBA_8888).setOpaque(false).setHidden(true).build(), and one Surface(child). Verify exact host generation, size and default display. Set position/crop and layer order relative only to siblings inside this host so the ordinary root guard, clipping, input and SystemUI ordering are preserved. Submit visible only under the normal current authorization, with a fresh empty child, without requiring a first-post callback round trip. Old children are never reused or re-shown. A late creation following terminal hide must release the unopened output without publishing it. No new accessibility window.

Keep full-colored buffers off the original SurfaceHolder even on the first poster. The framework SurfaceView can synchronize relayout to buffers on its own queue. Supply an explicitly transparent host buffer on its real creation/required redraw (coalesce compatible outstanding callbacks), using the existing worker and a host-bound gate. On a current redraw honor the actual framework redraw contract, including host participation and first valid child content; cancel/complete stale requests exactly once. Transparent host work is tied to holder lifecycle, never the animation cadence. Exercise both ordinary and synchronized redraw on the real system. Deadlock, black shell, hidden child, broken guard or repeated per-frame shell posts is a panel failure. Do not patch around it with timeouts or unhide the old host. Keep one LIVE child producer, one current host and bounded retired handles; record peak lifetime counts and preserve the existing single-worker policy. Under rapid churn cancel superseded unopened outputs and retire old ones without allowing a queue of externally visible generations.

B. At the normal worker draw boundary borrow the current target/surface through its existing access guard. Lock/draw/post against that same owner in try/finally. Preserve the painter, hardware canvas, phase, semitransparent edges, static first poster and single post/release on all exception paths. A late previously entered operation may finish only against its own output. It cannot submit visibility or target G2. Do not block Main on a new fence, await a compositor callback before executing the hide, or remove the existing holder-destruction safety for the shell. Ensure no native handle is closed during an entered operation or an outstanding copy. Retain the old owner until the asynchronous references have dropped, then unlink/release it exactly once, including errors and disposal. Use a bounded retiring slot and explicit backpressure: if it is still occupied by an older native borrower when a further target must be replaced, seal/hide all affected output, fail closed via the established withdrawal, cancel unopened successor work, finish already-entered borrowers exactly once, and let existing fresh admission restore later. Never queue an unbounded list of layers, closures or monitor waiters. Do not release the framework parent handle obtained from the view.

C. Main's retire primitive is idempotent and operates on the captured generation. Synchronously revoke admission first. While that generation's child control is still valid, issue a single immediate SurfaceControl.Transaction().setVisibility(child,false).apply() on that child; do not defer it to worker work, the next View draw, removeViewImmediate, or any commit callback. Keep a receipt for submission and optional transaction-committed callback (API35). Close the transaction on all paths. On real hide continue original root-local hide/removal; on FULL→discreet continue existing permitted neutral guard and new-generation setup. Apply the same retirement ordering on config switch, unexpected failure and disconnect. Invalid parent or submission failure goes directly to the existing safe local hide/removal/Fluvi surface failure pathway. Never replay old FULL, never report a failed attempt as a submitted/committed hide. A commit receipt and physical pixels are separate observations.

For guarded downgrade redirect the existing producer check from PixelCopy.request(SurfaceView,...) to the actual generation-owned output Surface; otherwise it reads the transparent shell. Hold the specific output reference until completion/error. Check target, privacy, guard, lease/generation and retest isCurrent before any guard retirement. Fail closed on stale/ambiguous content. Keep the existing producer shape checks and require positive permitted neutral output in the downgrade fixture; alpha and corners alone cannot distinguish FULL. Never use a screenshot or the host test classifier as runtime authority.

D. Diagnostics travel with the change in the same binary. ### What changed at the two architectural boundaries

- Before the ten-build window the lock-screen renderer migrated from main-thread View drawing to a separate GPU producer using HardwareBufferRenderer and SurfaceControl. Before migration, dc591498's wake-callback-to-live series was 569/139/208/314 and callback-to-local-hide was 123/12/196/79. On e7905b63 after migration the corresponding series were 421/299/206/268 and 7/22/19/14. The owner saw the ORB appear earlier but disappear late. The rendering endpoint changed from a View draw to isolated CPU submission; the separate runs support the user verdict and observed internal improvements, not a uniform causal speedup. The old first SCREEN_ON arrived after root draw and its 31 ms is not used for this comparison.
- R12 explicitly replaced the custom buffer-slot/first-offer/pressure-View chain with a platform SurfaceView queue for the eligible standalone ORB and changed bounded admission scheduling. The R11 first-live rows and R12 first-poster rows have different meanings. The R12 Surface build still yielded a 527 ms actual callback-to-local hide (228 ms inspection, 255 ms worker-to-Main delivery, 2 ms decision to local) and a 102 ms producer gap in FULL. Its separate LIGHT capture had no producer gap above 50 ms but still showed lag. R16 subsequently changed ownership/retirement of a generation-specific compositor child within this Surface route. It retained ordinary initial root acquisition. R08–R11 also changed fallback, buffer lifetime and first-frame delivery; these should not be counted as four renderer migrations.

### Reviewer interpretation

1. The one first-attachment app marker on R08/R09/R10/R11 fell from 1749 to 1433 to 788 to 225 ms (274 in the repeat on the same R11). The extreme startup stall improved in these samples. Ordinary wakes did not improve monotonically, and R11's two same-source runs differed substantially.
2. Within the more comparable LIGHT / Surface / actual full series, the first changed post in the initial retained wake measured 695 → 278 → 254 ms on R12/R13/R14. For the three later retained wakes per build, medians were 246 → 185 → 251 ms. R13's 61 ms lower median did not persist on R14. Conditions were not paired. The latest FULL/discreet capture is listed separately.
3. Local withdrawal alone understates the user experience. On R14 for example the three later accessibility events already took 74/81/77 ms to reach Fluvi. On R13 two withdrawals spent 130/174 ms in window inspection before local hide. On R16 first admission spent 150/29/122/174 ms in the active-root call, then another 99/77/84/123 ms between the show decision and first producer post. Physical keyguard onset and first/last visible ORB pixels remain unobserved throughout the comparison. The evidence establishes improved individual stages, persistent initial and warm lag, and no sustained user-accepted fix for lock/unlock synchrony.

Pinned source for the original measurements: 08fc46de46775b154a284621ef316b96404daf67 in this journal. Relevant lines: 3207–3225 and 4407–4428 (earlier isolation comparison), 10131–10142 and 10242–10256 (R06/R07), 10515–10527 (R08), 10785–10801 (R09), 11046–11073 (R10), 11502–11512 (both R11 captures), 11781–11788 and 11917–11928 (R12), 11958–11965 and 12584 (R13), 12542–12556 (R14), 13208–13221 (R16 and original pasted episode times). This historical clarification does not supersede or expand the R17 execution contract.

PROVEN: multiple additive sequential stages recur. Three slow R16 initial physical active-root calls, the ordinary initial host/first-frame tail on all four, and large Main scheduling delays on individual samples are independently timed. Same R11 binary had warm wake-to-live 297/332/340 ms after inconclusive first inspections and 103/144/135 ms following first-read MAIN in its repeat. UNPROVEN: how much interruptible root acquisition saves on this handset, how much prewarming survives a cold wake, whether a black rectangle comes from a particular layer, and whether earlier local withdrawal tracks the perceived unlock. MISSING: independent time-aligned first/last correct images at physical transitions, OEM signal latency before event creation and matched same-disclosure candidate comparisons.
