The current asset SHA-256 values in order are ebf3629b7f723113ea9f13a89fc37c52ec2f9a4db2fc4e64b901dc1a622b61f2, c777abadfdfd6c778a37b7448cc8b7943a1ca3a086676e7b47360be008f62f4b and 5d85bad2c00e4a6ab680b843fe68cb9265dccb7d2af3e6acbe5d9e9528d4c674. The reviewer selects the architecture and the product owner accepts physical behavior.

## 4. Physical feedback and the two clocks

The owner observes fast disappearance on unlock and late appearance when the lockscreen wakes. Treat the current handset as one observation. Keep two user-facing measurements: (1) physical wake stimulus to the first correct visible ORB; (2) first visible eligible main-lockscreen frame to the first correct visible ORB. Measure both from the same wake. The first includes panel wake and system scheduling. The second describes whether the ORB pops in after the rest of the lockscreen. The architecture targets the very same eligible frame. The 10 ms ceiling remains a maximum. A p95, an app callback, a neutral placeholder or one successful device cannot substitute for either optical result.

## 5. Evidence and clock audit

R22.4 primary evidence is the owner-pasted LIGHT capture 97908f95-517d-41d1-b71f-6c3ebc81d98c and FULL capture 846f48d4-e1d9-441b-92d9-707504e15be4, both from the same already-connected process. Four direct winners were retained per capture. Both exports were truncated. Physical wake, first and last pixel were unobserved.

| Elapsed from the app's first wake callback (ms) | LIGHT 1 / 4 / 5 / 6 | FULL 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 |
|---|---|---|
| Final showing read completed | 604 / 342 / 337 / 341 | 299 / 149 / 270 / 314 |
| Accepted native reveal call returned | 652 / 387 / 374 / 375 | 321 / 200 / 312 / 357 |

FULL 1 is the discriminating case. Hidden host bound at +43 ms, final showing read finished at +299, proof accepted at +300, first buffer ready at +305, native transaction returned at +321 and first distinct motion was submitted at +330. The worker found the bitmap in its in-process map. The 5 ms is a single proof-to-buffer interval that includes work beyond lookup. There is no disk-read measurement here. Shutdown and wake paths run concurrently with other work, so subtract matching same-wake endpoints and do not add nested scopes.

## 6. History and what changed the decision

R18 reduced layer creation work; its initial FULL route prepared the discreet image. R19 prepared a blank FULL-capable target. R20 drew directly on a first-image miss. R21 kept an already submitted reveal through eligible rechecks. R22 added a bounded transfer between readers and captured later superseding requests. R22.4 also addressed an isolated output/parent retirement issue. R22.5 did not obtain calibrated emulator frames. Its marker experiment did not ship in the phone build. R23 proposed one further reader transfer. The three observed obsolete B tails left at most 63, 30 and 67 ms of that B work before completion. Even deleting that whole observed tail in each case accounts for only 20 ms averaged over the eight retained slots, before other scheduling effects. The comparable small LIGHT groups for R18, R21 and R22.4 averaged 377.5, 395.5 and 447 ms to native submit/return as recorded in the R23 review. No controlled average speedup or optical deadline compliance has been established.

## 7. Source and dependency provenance

The matching graph is tooling commit f28fadc75e399868b8541a7d5617977b2a7de877. Its manifest SHA-256 is 63772aeb51033d51b8c2278137bd2286b7086d46b3e4b8b9324ff24e669f7b71. It indexes the app source; the Kotlin inventory and source define the native edges. The ownership boundary leads outside this app repository into the OS keyguard compositor. The repository contains no shippable control of device SystemUI or panel firmware.

## 8. Current source facts and prior art in Fluvi

Under android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen, FluviKeyguardCardService.readSystemWindows/inspectSurface obtain scene evidence, KeyguardFirstAuthorizedOrb.offer/consume validate the current request, scene and revisions, and advanceR19First joins proof and readiness. material/KeyguardOrbR18Presenter prepares and retires the owned surface; material/KeyguardOrbSurfaceWorker indexes posters and draws an authorized hit or miss. A fresh external scene can invalidate the proof even if the pixels are ready. The public locked bit includes occlusion and screen-off states.

Fluvi already builds frame sequences off-thread for the launcher. widget/orb/FluviOrbWidget.kt, FluviOrbWidgetProvider.render, checks each configured generation, constructs RemoteViews and publishes with AppWidgetManager.updateAppWidget. The widget host advances the sequence. res/xml/fluvi_orb_widget_info.xml describes the home provider; res/xml/fluvi_financial_snapshot_widget_info.xml declares a different provider for home and keyguard. The home ORB options do not encode the lockscreen FULL disclosure policy. Provider metadata cannot establish which host owns the first lockscreen frame or certify what that frame contained.

## 9. Proven, unproven and missing

PROVEN in the observed build: all eight first-positive request IDs differed from the consumed request; seven rejections recorded SCENE_CHANGED and one NEWER_READ_REQUIRED. Final showing reads took place well before the accepted native reveal, including on a cache hit. PROVEN platform constraint: Android 15, 16 and 17 CDD §3.8.2 makes lockscreen app-widget support optional. Host placement and entry trigger belong to the host. Android app processes may be reclaimed. UNPROVEN: which individual OS/app operation determined the first optical pixel on any wake, or whether every newer inspection was avoidable. MISSING: an Android-wide API for a normal app to participate with scene-appropriate content in the initial main-keyguard composition with a 10 ms physical deadline. No further capture on one model can establish a universal platform contract.

## 10. Architecture decision

Move the decision to include the ORB into the component that composes the lockscreen. Move first-frame production to content changes. A system implementation of both sides could remove wake-time Fluvi scheduling, window inspection, fresh surface creation, full-image drawing and a separate reveal transaction from the first-frame dependency chain. This is the selected design for simultaneous lockscreen appearance. Implementing it solely inside exptv2 cannot make the unmodified Android installations in the product population implement the required host. Even an integrated host would still need a separate panel/input timing commitment to guarantee 10 ms from physical wake.

## 11. Delivery scope and existing app users

One Android contract, with no manufacturer checks or per-model timeouts. A capable installed host could support simultaneous appearance. A widget picker entry, home AppWidget support, an SDK version check, an app-owned window, or an assumed permanently resident service cannot establish that capability. The existing overlay can remain a compatibility route with measured latency and privacy characteristics. Users on that route remain in the denominator of the universal product claim. A provider that only appears after a swipe, while docked, or after an async host request also fails ordinary wake-first placement. A custom OS image would reach only its installed population and constitutes a separate delivery decision.

## 12. Ownership and lifecycle

| Boundary and current owner | Proposed transition and consumer | Risk and required control |
|---|---|---|
| Visual revision: lockscreen material/profile producer; home provider is a separate consumer | On data, palette, mode, scope, density, size or policy revision, a bounded worker produces the correct first picture and continuation parameters. Publish a complete immutable generation to a trusted system host in advance. | Late production completion must not replace a newer revision. Reject wrong user, display or policy epoch. Keep the home provider isolated. |
| First frame: KeyguardFirstAuthorizedOrb + app-owned surface | The host holds prepared content for the enrolled user and display. In its own scene commit it selects FULL, permitted neutral, or absent. | A locked bit cannot distinguish an incoming call or credentials. FULL requires explicit user policy and a matching host-owned eligible scene at composition. |
| Retirement: KeyguardOrbR18Presenter.seal and worker | Within the same host scene transition remove detailed content on shade, credentials, occlusion, unlock or privacy restriction. Invalidate outstanding generations before reuse. | Static and moving pixels share the same parent and visibility decision. No cached detailed surface above a restricted scene, secondary overlay or late old buffer. |
| First motion: KeyguardOrbSurfaceWorker on the app route | The host continues the accepted generation from the same phase on its next eligible presentation. Advance with the visible frame clock. | No second attach, reset or flash. Pause offscreen, on screen-off and on reduced-motion settings. Test the first moving frame separately from first appearance. |
| Host/process loss or switch | Retire/dispose old ownership. Recover only a still-authorized, current generation, otherwise render the allowed neutral/absent state while re-priming. | Bound memory to current plus in-flight replacement until compositor release. Process death, reboot before first unlock, user switch, data/day rollover and trim must never resurrect private imagery. A late or missing full first frame stays a miss. |

## 13. Falsification controls for an actual future host

For a future integrator, the structural positives are (a) a current, prepublished FULL generation in the very first eligible scene frame while the app is asleep, and (b) showing the same current generation where policy permits after a normal app-process kill without a wake-time callback. Separate cold unprimed, immediately superseded, stale private, hidden and restricted cases. Switch to credentials, incoming-call occlusion, shade and another user with a FULL frame queued. Inspect the composed frame at transition. Include rapid wake/unlock/relock and loss of the host. A stale FULL pixel fails privacy; a neutral or missing FULL on an eligible wake fails the performance sample. One violation disproves a claimed hard bound.

## 14. Proposed host contract

These are proposed operations, not Android SDK APIs. Prepublication carries visual generation, user/display identity, size/density, data/policy revisions, prepared pixels and animation phase. The trusted host installs a complete generation atomically and acknowledges receipt before readiness is recorded. A restrictive transition always wins over a queued publication. Revoke, replace and release are idempotent and keyed by generation. Keep detailed content private to the enrolled system keyguard; the integrity of an arbitrary widget host or a widget option alone cannot authorize financial data. Keep both disk I/O and the Fluvi process outside the warm first-frame path. Avoid continuous offscreen animation. No duplicated app overlay in the integrated route.

## 15. Performance and acceptance

Record physical wake-to-ORB, optical main-lockscreen-to-ORB and first distinct motion separately. Use a common-timed external wake marker and sufficiently fast camera or photodiodes with known errors. Compare lockscreen and ORB at the same scanline or compensate for scanout. Identify the *correct* visible content with a synthetic test pattern. If the upper uncertainty bound crosses 10 ms, classify the sample as inconclusive; a demonstrated violation fails. Report every eligible wake, missing content, first/cold and warm populations, refresh mode, motion cadence, maximum and uncertainty. Atomic same-frame inclusion is a frame-identity result independent of time spent waking a powered-off display. A single handset, emulator screenshot, app callback or commit receipt cannot certify every Android device.

## 16. Order and migration

A platform integration would first require an identifiable trusted host with an actual first-scene composition and revocation hook and a deployable system delivery path. Next establish source-level ownership and compare the above positive and exclusion fixtures using synthetic content. Then connect the app's revision producer to that host, make cutover mutually exclusive with the existing overlay, and restore the original route if the integration is disabled. Host loss fails closed before re-entry through any other route. A change of delivery scope or of the universal 10 ms requirement belongs to the product owner. No such change has been assumed.

## 2026-11-22 — R24 design review of the first visible lockscreen frame

The owner retained a normally installed APK, the ordinary wake screen on Android phones across manufacturers, the existing animated financial ORB and a maximum visible lag of 10 ms. The follow-up asks for design. R23 remains superseded. This entry refines R24 at the SystemUI composition boundary. It authorizes no change of distribution, no application implementation and no test build.

### Evidence and scope

The phone-tested R22.4 profile and implementation ref still identify `ad1eac09442cb8d78a992874d22157fe6bd5a05f`. Coordination at review time was `09a33d0933178ffde5e0d4300a70dd80c574797d`, a 118-line journal-only addition following `60f96ab6584952d9964550a43da723278f6c8091`. The coordination and application branches have diverged. Main was `fe10593ec833e41080186404c053e81e5889d623`. The named R23/R24/R25 remote-ref search found no new implementation for these designs. The pre-review coordination SHA returned zero workflow runs. Matching tooling `f28fadc75e399868b8541a7d5617977b2a7de877` identifies the exact source. Its Dart SCIP graph and native symbol inventory have different coverage. Native conclusions here were checked in Kotlin. See the R22.4 and R22.5 qualification reports and the two captures identified in the preceding R24 entry. This follow-up received no new raw capture or physical outcome.

**PROVEN.** In FULL capture attempt 1 the hidden target was bound at +43 ms, the grant was accepted at +300 ms, the buffer was ready at +305 ms, the native reveal returned at +321 ms and distinct motion was first submitted at +330 ms. All are relative to that wake's app callback. The hit was an in-process bitmap lookup. Five milliseconds characterizes the interval from grant to buffer in that attempt. Across the eight retained attempts the final showing read finished at +149 to +604 ms. Inspection and graphics can overlap. A zero-cost first draw after the same grant would still leave that grant on the critical path. **UNPROVEN.** The precise physical pop-in time, or how much of the wait a particular device's OS contributed. **MISSING.** A deployable public contract giving a third-party APK authority to put the correctly disclosed ORB in the first main-keyguard composition on all target phones.

### Ownership and concrete reference boundary

Android 15, 16 and 17 CDD §3.8.2 leaves keyguard widgets optional. The OEM can choose a charging/docking trigger. Android 17 general handheld AppWidget support does not imply an ordinary wake-screen host. API 34 `AccessibilityService.attachAccessibilityOverlayToWindow` attaches to a window and tracks geometry. A single SystemUI window can contain the keyguard, credential UI and shade. The public live wallpaper route occupies the selected wallpaper slot and its destination flags identify which screen(s) it serves. Those contracts give Fluvi neither frame-specific financial disclosure nor a universal first-frame guarantee.

The reference is AOSP `platform/frameworks/base`, release `android-16.0.0_r1`. In `packages/SystemUI/compose/features/src/com/android/systemui/keyguard/ui/composable/`, `LockscreenScene.kt` hands off to `LockscreenContent.kt` and its selected blueprint. In `packages/SystemUI/src/com/android/systemui/keyguard/shared/model/KeyguardState.kt`, `mapToSceneContainerContent()` maps OFF, DOZING, DREAMING, AOD, ALTERNATE_BOUNCER, OCCLUDED and LOCKSCREEN to the same scene key. Primary credentials map to a separate overlay. Therefore even an integrated build must resolve the actual composition and transition, including overlaid or occluding content. The scene key, the window ID and an earlier asynchronous state snapshot are insufficient. The older View blueprint has a different binding route. The reference names describe one release and imply no stable SDK ABI.

### Proposed design if a platform distributor supplies this host

| Boundary | Proposed behavior | Guard and discriminating check |
|---|---|---|
| Content production. The current worker and `KeyguardOrbSurfacePainter` receive immutable profile copies and produce visuals. | Publish on changes to the configured material, data, mode/scope/category, policy or display geometry. Package a correct transparent frame at a defined phase, versioned animation parameters and the user/display/revision identities. The trusted host preloads both frame and continuation resources before acknowledging readiness. | Two out-of-order publications, a geometry change, process death after acknowledgment and an unsupported effect version. Older work cannot supersede the latest accepted generation. User configuration and the existing home widget remain independent. |
| First composition. The app route's `readSystemWindows`, `inspectSurface`, `KeyguardFirstAuthorizedOrb.offer/consume` and `advanceR19First` join fresh evidence to prepared output. | In the reference design a non-interactive ORB slot draws inside the host's own lockscreen root. The same frame decision that draws the eligible main lockscreen includes the ready ORB. No app callback, Binder round trip to Fluvi, first-time upload, disk access or new app window may gate that frame. The host proceeds immediately if the ORB is missing. | Trace the first eligible system composition with Fluvi's process absent. It must contain the correct enrolled generation. An absent, stale or neutral ORB on an eligible FULL wake counts as a miss. The lockscreen clock and controls must appear on time even if Fluvi is stalled. |
| First motion. The existing painter accepts independent elapsed and phase values for the base, background and interior. | Prewarm a fixed, versioned host renderer for supported Fluvi material effects. Render the first picture at the specified phase, then advance the same generation on the host's visible-frame clock. Pick the first live delta from the first presented phase. The host accepts typed parameters only and executes its own renderer. | Compare the first correct image and first genuinely changed frame separately against the source visual at matched phases. Exercise normal motion, configured static material, reduced motion, hide/re-entry and a revision arriving between the two frames. No phase reset, duplicate overlay or busy offscreen animation. |
| Exit, restrictions and restoration. The app route currently invalidates its grant and seals the output. | The same authoritative host composition removes FULL on the first restrictive frame, even when the outgoing lockscreen still animates underneath. Use the existing discreet/absent policy as appropriate. Unlock, shade, credential entry, occlusion, an unknown state, user change or policy withdrawal cannot inherit a prior grant. A canceled transition restores FULL only on a newly eligible composition. | Open credentials or shade, occlude with a call, and rapidly unlock/relock with an old FULL generation pending. Check the composed pixels and input pass-through. Reclaim old buffers after the consumer releases them. |
| Loss and change of owner. | Keep the host's accepted generation private to its user and display, bounded to the active package and one in-flight replacement. Invalidate on policy tightening, user switch, app removal or host reset. Use a host-enforced validity boundary for clock/day-sensitive data. The proposed slot must be under the same disclosure and frame authority as any separately composed occluding layer. If the candidate OS tree cannot coordinate those changes in the same composition, the host is unqualified. Merely adding a Composable to the blueprint does not satisfy this condition. Neither a timeout waiting for ORB readiness nor delaying the clock to make the ORB seem simultaneous is permitted.

### Acceptance and delivery decision

Measure four separate endpoints in each eligible trial. (1) Physical wake stimulus to first correct ORB pixel. (2) First visible main-keyguard reference to first correct ORB pixel. (3) First correct ORB to the first visually distinct animated frame when animation is enabled. (4) First visible restrictive/unlock transition to disappearance of FULL. A composition identifier can establish co-membership of the ORB and clock. For optical timing use a common-timed stimulus and external camera/photodiodes, same-scanline reference or calibrated scanout offset, and a synthetic content revision distinguishable from neutral and stale imagery. Use traces for stage attribution. Record all misses and uncertainty. An upper bound at or below 10 ms passes that sample, a lower bound above 10 ms fails, overlap is inconclusive. One delayed refresh costs about 16.67 ms at 60 Hz or 8.33 ms at 120 Hz. Evaluate first-frame membership separately from the numerical limit.

If an integrated reference host is ever provided, the initial finite comparison on each supported test configuration is four warm, two process-absent/primed and two cold/unprimed ordinary wakes, plus one each for the credential, shade, call-occlusion and rapid unlock/relock controls. Include four matched ORB-disabled ordinary wakes as controls for delaying the keyguard itself. A guaranteed deadline cannot be established by these samples. Report every slot, the maximum with uncertainty and the applied frame identity. A forbidden FULL pixel or any demonstrated overrun rejects the corresponding claim. A host absent from stock phones is a distribution constraint even if the reference build passes.

With the owner's current scope, the actionable reviewer decision is to keep R23 superseded and decline a universal-deadline app build. ## 8. CURRENT SOURCE FACTS

K/FluviKeyguardCardService.kt uses `Dispatchers.IO.limitedParallelism(1)`. `processInspectionQueue` completes a real read, tries the R12 policy, and normally awaits `withContext(Dispatchers.Main.immediate) { applyCompletedInspection(...) }` before `inspectionQueue.complete(active)`. K/KeyguardCardInspectionQueue.kt `KeyguardReadAheadPolicy.rejection` accepts a narrowly defined complete negative with NO_MAIN_MARKER. It rejects a complete SHOW_FULL. An offered request can therefore already invalidate the preceding positive via `firstAuthorizedOrb.requireRead` or scene invalidation, yet that stale positive can still hold the worker and enter Main admission. On the staged path its proof can then be rejected in `prepareR18Decision`.

The existing R22 transfer happens *inside* an in-progress reader under special conditions. R25 changes the ownership boundary *after* a complete positive read. R12 ordered negative read-ahead, R14 recovery and decisive exclusion keep their existing semantics. The presenter preparation at `KeyguardCardWindow.prepareR18` is exact-SDK-35 code. The common reader and generic Main apply serve other configurations. Implement R25 in the common opening queue according to actual mode, visibility and ownership. Keep renderer capability checks at their existing boundaries. Do not extend SDK-35 graphics calls to other releases or branch on manufacturer/model.

## 8. CURRENT SOURCE FACTS

1. reduceR25 uses putIfAbsent for backend and parkedOriginal. A summary can retain A after discard or supersession. r25PostDrain can later claim the latest waiting ticket for its notice. A retained R25_CORE parked=A and a matching authority do not establish that A was still waiting when the command was issued. The DIRECT observer already reads the real waiting ticket under the queue lock.
2. The shade fixture's collector runs freely while the instrumentation thread polls count >=4, queries visibleShade and posts the release to Main. A fifth screenshot can complete in that interval. The corrected grader requires exactly four. Millisecond ties between the end of frame four and the start of release can occur.
3. evaluate assigns a single mutually exclusive relation and drops STRADDLES_RELEASE from its relevant set. The physical acquisition interval can span release while lying wholly after shade or even after current exclusion. The privacy meaning and scheduling meaning are independent.
4. The shade post-control reconnects an already locked service and expects STOCK. In original run 45022727111 this setup produced a genuine R18_DIRECT positive. The new warm witness observed STOCK after connecting unlocked and then performing a sleep/wake. Both routes are real and neither is an interchangeable control.
5. KeyguardR251DirectInstrumentationTest uses a boolean across two automation.windows enumerations, with just three main markers and four shade markers. Queries with unavailable roots or exceptions become false. Production has fuller marker sets and treats incomplete observations as unknown. The raw combined failure cannot isolate a platform fault or route defect.

## 2026-11-22 — Wake-to-ORB below 100 ms: design and go/no-go criteria

Owner asks how to reduce the roughly 300 ms visible delay. This design review follows R26 (7fbf9706f1227ec8e3b6e0bd6af2e57003fe9b26). R26 remains the independent DIRECT withdrawal-containment experiment. No additional app, test, dispatch or new build is part of this entry. The engineering target is below 100 ms on measured configurations. Retain the historical inclusive 100 ms result separately if a bracket touches exactly 100 ms.

**Evidence.** The first physical window *read* started 5, 6, 15 and 6 ms after the application wake callback in R25 LIGHT capture 8703ccf9-bae0-4cdf-86a5-0d023afdfc66. The first accepted current proof arrived at +945, +328, +174 and +207 ms (attempts 1,7,8,9). Native reveal apply returned at +1082, +393, +223 and +275 ms. First proof to native return was therefore 137/65/49/68 ms. Those intervals include scheduling and, in attempts 7 and 9, validation of a subsequent request. Host bound before first proof in all four. All four records say DIRECT_MISS. These application intervals establish which stages matter. They do not date first physical exposure or the earliest evidence Android could have supplied. An earlier R22.4 bitmap hit reached a ready buffer about 5 ms after authorization and still took 321 ms from callback to native reveal return.

**Budget and comparison.** Initial *design allocations*, not predictions: aim for at most 55 ms from the selected external start through obtaining and accepting a complete current proof, 15 ms more to the first correctly painted buffer and 25 ms more to the observed first correct pixel. The remaining 5 ms is margin. Account for callback delivery and scanout against the total. Buffers, callbacks and frame commits do not satisfy the optical endpoint. Keep independent per-trial results for physical wake stimulus and for first visible eligible lockscreen frame. Pair app timestamps to a common optical reference with a measured alignment error; a missing stimulus marker can leave the first verdict open while the second is scorable.

**First lever — stop using the one reader for work that can no longer open the current scene.** At exact R25, KeyguardWindowSnapshotReader.visibleIds marks a missing advertised child as truncated and can continue to visit other nodes. In attempt 1 the first advertised child was null, the incomplete A lasted 137 ms, and the eventual showing request was 13. In 7 the early reader already yielded. In 8 and 9 it completed after newer offers and its guard recorded an aggregate disqualifier. These are different cases. Do not infer a removable 137 ms or treat every event as a reason to cancel. R23's limited B→C transfer had a small historical ceiling.

Compare these paths on one exact input/time sequence: existing complete classification, a fail-closed retirement of an irreversibly incomplete opening scan when a genuine newer current request is waiting, and the natural unheld run. For the candidate, consider only a verified hidden virgin FULL route with no retained proof, painted output, grant or pending reveal. Under the existing queue authority, make the old generation ineligible to authorize or publish. Retain observed exclusions, apply fail-closed safeguards and preserve any required cache clear. After the in-flight call returns and all borrowed nodes have been recycled, give the *one* reader to the actual latest request. Require a fresh complete inventory, tree and policy decision for that request before any FULL paint, demand or reveal. A building, submitted or visible FULL, ambiguous ownership, stale route, unmatched age or absent successor takes the established path. No prior-wake approval, event-only positive, parallel tree walkers, quiet timer or unbounded restarts. Start with one permitted transfer per wake shared with the existing opening-yield allowance. A stopped scan is neither a negative proof of shade absence nor a successful show.

Use the existing non-actuating reader/fixture evidence to reconstruct physical callback, root/child, invalidation, first permanently incomplete point, eligible successor, accepted proof, buffer and native edges, plus optical frames when available. Compare the same captured input sequences to isolate avoidable work; compare actual unheld runs to see whether the final correct pixel moves. Where no successor was waiting or earlier complete observations are missing, record zero demonstrated saving or unknown. If the available saving is small or the safe proof is still late, do not promote this optimization as the 100 ms solution. A recorded late first proof alone cannot establish public SDK impossibility.

**Second lever — move program preparation off the authorized first paint.** On a DIRECT_MISS the animated worker constructs KeyguardOrbSurfacePainter, which constructs KeyguardHeaderShader via its context constructor. This calls AndroidKeyguardShaderArtifactReader.load and creates a RuntimeShader. Reuse the existing prepared immutable shader artifact when keyed to the exact effect/portal variant and asset revision. Prepare at most one never-configured program on its owning worker before wake when feasible. At the actual grant, apply the current size, phase, profile and authorized financial uniforms. Keep the hidden target virgin, without a previous FULL image or private uniforms. Preserve the cold path, effect changes, process restart, static/unsupported effects, pressure and teardown. Use existing R20 entry/painter/configure/lock/draw/post intervals, warm/cold and byte/pixel controls. A successful object construction does not establish that the driver precompiled every GPU step. Count savings only on the observed first correct picture. Skip this optimization if the measured constructor/load slice cannot materially move it.

**Decision and product boundary.** Use equal settings and bounded ABBA blocks, including ordinary warm wakes, first cold wake and rapid unlock/relock. Preserve wrong or late frames and trial maxima; a timed-out blank, stale generation, neutral placeholder, shade/credential disclosure or delayed unlock invalidates the corresponding success claim. Use simple ordinary-wake phone feedback for visible quality and calibrated external capture for a numerical claim. Assess all tested configurations individually. Do not assume a paired average qualifies the maximum. Where evidence establishes that the app cannot obtain current sufficient Android information with enough time for that trial, that trial is beyond the proposed verifier's budget. A general cross-OEM deadline is unavailable through the audited SDK contract. The architecture capable of eliminating the app-side authorization round trip is the R24 integrated SystemUI design: publish a revision-tagged ORB on data/material changes, let the trusted system host include it in the same first eligible composition and revoke it in the first restrictive composition. This needs a distributable host and OS/OEM support. The physical wake-to-panel delay is still independent. Platform references: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/KeyguardManager#isKeyguardLocked() and https://source.android.com/docs/compatibility/16/android-16-cdd#3_8_2_widgets.

FluviKeyguardCardService.processInspectionQueue publishes completed reads. R25 may promote a pending read or park the completed result on STOCK and DIRECT. ## 14. IMPLEMENTATION AND DIAGNOSTIC CONTRACT

A. Apply R26 §§12–14 in full. For a matching complete DIRECT positive return ordinary dispatch with DIRECT_ORDERED before constructing an R25 ticket, suppressing, promoting or parking. In processInspectionQueue use withContext(Dispatchers.Main.immediate) → applyCompletedInspection → inspectionQueue.complete(active) → scheduleR19Join. Restrict r25CompatibleLocked to matching STOCK. Leave terminal seal/retire path independent; include R26's compact proof/receipt/withdrawal evidence and exact winning seal cause. Already landed equivalent code counts after verification.

B. Carry a typed incomplete-walk reason through visibleIds, the checkpoint and the yielded result. Allow the new reason only after a successful advertised child acquisition returns null, while the only incompleteness is that kind of missing child. Track independently of capture/timing.invalid. Exceptions, limits, abort, prior incomplete inventory or ambiguous ownership retain established behavior. At a genuine remaining beforeChild boundary after the in-flight IPC has returned and observed exclusion markers have been consumed, consult the existing lightweight hint. Require the positively identified active SystemUI root, existing cleanOpeningInventory, exact ownership and no decisive restriction. Otherwise continue/seal normally. Keep the original !truncated path. Avoid taking queueLock on every child without a hint.

Under queueLock recheck the real opportunity/token, reservation, service, route, wake and interaction/attachment/visibility authority, exact current scene, genuine framework ingress ID and actual latest pending request ID, established freshness including any required cache clear. For the new reason require a detached virgin DIRECT target and reject any retained/current proof, requested/in-progress/submitted paint, pending reveal, showing/visible output or financial grant; use existing synchronized reservation/proof state and invalidation, never unsynchronized worker fields. Only on full match atomically call queue.handoffOpening(A,B), consume the existing single allowance, and keep the actual offer's requireRead(B.id). Revoke A's ability to complete/apply without invalidating the common reservation needed by B. Bubble yieldedTo through reader Result → InspectionOutcome.Yielded → PhysicalReadOutcome.Yielded, including the typed reason and true partial status, bypass classification/admission of A, unwind all owned nodes/roots, then start B on the same reader. Verify readStarted/readFinished and cleanup ownership on cancellation/teardown. No recursive B→C and no request inferred from time proximity.

C. In the retained LIVE path derive only the existing public program selector (effectId, profile.usesPortal, and the painter's static-gradient predicate). In the virgin FULL DIRECT preparation pass that selector separately; keep the worker target's profile argument null. Put a lazy KeyguardShaderArtifactStore under the retained LIVE presenter lifecycle; it must work when the separate View material controller is disposed. Reuse AndroidKeyguardShaderArtifactReader and KeyguardHeaderShader(artifact). Accept only exact selector, metadata revision and verified artifact.programKey (effect/portal/generated AGSL hash/adapter version); unknown or mismatched metadata takes the normal cold route. Handle synchronous cached and asynchronous Main callback paths without constructing a shader on Main. Keep at most one active request plus one coalesced latest desired selector and one unused never-configured program on the existing renderer worker. Check request/owner epoch even across A→B→A, current target/lease and disposal. Post back from store to the owning worker. Use its detached idle opportunity after allocation/created, before wake where available. Never enqueue speculative work ahead of revocation, required blank binding or a pending authorized paint. No FULL pixels, balance values, palettes, uniforms, bitmap, canvas or running animation are required to prepare program code.

At actual prepareAuthorized, after current target/ticket checks and the established poster lookup, consume matching unused program once on the animated DIRECT_MISS path. Pass it to KeyguardOrbSurfacePainter, configure it only with this grant's current profile, dimensions and canonical first-frame time. Preserve actual BITMAP_HIT/legacy/static behavior, failed lock/post handling and later motion. The authorization increments preparationGeneration; the valid transition for this same owner must keep its slot usable. Missing or unready program takes existing cold construction immediately (an exact ready immutable artifact may supply source). Never wait for an asynchronous result or create/share a mutable shader across owners or with the View. A same-worker constructor already running cannot be preempted: check demand before/after it, reuse the completed exact match when valid, instrument overlap and queue delay. A stale/failed completion does not suppress the cold path; dispose store/queued request/unused program on owner loss or close, guard late insertions/callbacks, keep store lifetime bounded. Exclude candidate regressions from speed claims.

D. Export compact optional attempt-scoped scalars in the same Human APK: read/first permanent incomplete reason, real B pending time/ID, eligibility or first rejection, claim and read boundaries, first accepted versus actually consumed proof, ticket, warm selector/status/cold reason, load/constructor/worker queue and R20 painter/configure/lock/draw/post spans, native final reveal/retire receipts and original hide cause. Counters for eligible, yielded, warm-hit, no-ready, stale and overlap. Use existing uptimeMs for lifecycle, System.nanoTime for worker/render spans and existing per-generation clock alignment/uncertainty for compositor. Attach capture/session/wake/attachment/reservation/owner IDs. Preserve absent fields, no per-node chatter, no additional framework queries or disk writing on the critical path. Grade diagnostic loss separately.

## 15. PERFORMANCE GATE

Two independent strict maxima per tested configuration: physical wake stimulus → first optically correct FULL ORB pixel; first visible eligible ordinary lockscreen frame → same pixel. Record actual unlock-animation onset → last visible ORB and first confirmed absent as a regression comparison to the preferred baseline. Calibrate external video frame spacing, onset visibility, clock alignment and scanline uncertainty; visually confirm geometry, correct material and user-visible motion. For each interval, upper bound <100 ms passes that trial; lower bound >=100 fails; otherwise indeterminate. Missing onset leaves only that clock unscored. Give the historical inclusive threshold separately when material. Design allocations are 55 ms to a complete current proof, 15 ms more to correct paint, 25 ms more to first physical pixel, 5 ms margin. Never infer optical success from these allocations.

Use one matched unheld A/B/B/A series, two ordinary wakes per block, for principal R25 A vs combined B. Include matched unlock/relock. Record true cold and already-connected warm trials separately; keep all eight planned wakes, timeouts, worst case and paired deltas. No service restart between ordinary warm wakes. Compare R26-only intermediate via focused identical-input controls and record source provenance; compare preferred R22.4 withdrawal separately. A forced candidate path demonstrates mechanism, not frequency during ordinary use. Where public SDK evidence is too late for an observed trial, report that exact residual and what constraint would need to change. Faster buffers with no earlier final FULL do not meet the product goal.

The download issue is closed independently of the phone rejection. Previously preferred withdrawal comparator ad1eac09442cb8d78a992874d22157fe6bd5a05f is a reference, not evidence of a 10 ms solution.

**Why a resident picture helps and where it stops.** At exact R27, KeyguardOrbSurfaceWorker keeps at most two posters; KeyguardOrbSurfacePainter.makePoster creates a hardware bitmap. KeyguardOrbR18Presenter.seal calls revoke(discardFull = true) for the outgoing target; the worker discards FULL posters on that path. The ordinary virgin DIRECT target starts empty. R27 moves eligible shader code preparation earlier. It does not retain a ready-to-disclose private FULL picture across every lock/unlock. A true independent retained snapshot would be a different lifetime and would remove first-paint work on a hit. It could not grant permission to expose its contents.

The historical R22.4 FULL phone sample is the pertinent existing control: hidden host bound at app wake callback +43 ms, grant +300 ms, ready buffer from a real in-process bitmap hit +305 ms, native reveal returned +321 ms. These are app-side events in one trial, not screen pixels. R27's separate emulator service specimen reached accepted proof after 3826 ms, posted the first buffer roughly 7 ms from worker entry with a warm hit, and returned from native reveal at +3848 ms. Those data do not time the owner's new phone trial. Even zero-cost painting after the same observed grant cannot meet a ten-millisecond end-to-end bound in the historical phone trial under the same event order. This is not proof that Android could never supply adequate evidence earlier in any trial.

For exit, FluviKeyguardCardService.sealR18 already invalidates the proof and calls sealR18FromAnyThread; KeyguardOrbDirectOutput.retire posts hide/unparent at the front of its own queue ahead of ordinary Main host cleanup. Earlier R25 seal-to-native-return values were 0–3 ms. Earlier owner-visible unlock, first app-recognized restriction, transaction return, and actual last visible pixel are separately observable boundaries. In the R27 phone rejection the relative contributions of late indication, scheduling/contention, stale layer and scanout remain unknown. If an existing R27 capture/video becomes available, correlate original attachment and winning restriction with actual removal. No new phone log is a prerequisite to rejecting R27 or making the architectural decision.

**Reviewer decision.** R27 optimized within the app-observe → app-authorize → submit → system-compose path. It did not replace that path. Stop advancing the rejected line as the cross-OEM hard-deadline solution. The 10 ms maximum is a product criterion. A future trial on an individual device can pass it, but no audited ordinary SDK contract can reserve the finance ORB's place in every manufacturer's first ordinary lockscreen composition or its absence in the first restrictive composition. A system-side benchmark is a distinct distribution decision. An app overlay, a faster window reader, retaining a FULL bitmap forever or a guessed reveal from SCREEN_ON/isKeyguardLocked do not establish this contract. In particular, keyguard can report locked even when an incoming-call activity occludes it. fluvi_orb_widget_info.xml currently advertises home_screen. Registering another widget category on its own cannot supply a missing or differently triggered lockscreen widget host.

**Structural replacement if a distributable host exists.** Keep the R24 trusted-host design. Its concrete runtime contract is:

1. Off the wake path, a private publisher reacts to visual/data/configuration or privacy revision changes and produces a transparent ready-to-display first frame at a known phase plus parameters for motion. Identify user/profile, display/size and visual and policy revisions. Perform decode/upload before readiness. Host retains one acknowledged current resource and at most one replacement; accept monotonically and drop late publications. New policy revokes old content even while replacement work is pending. Loss of host state, unknown freshness and user switch invalidate eligibility. A process-local pointer alone is insufficient if the app has been reclaimed.
2. On wake, the component that composes the actual eligible ordinary lockscreen includes its acknowledged revision in that very composition. There is no app-side scene scan, new app window, IPC to a paused app or first-time paint on that critical path. After the first visible frame, advance motion from its actual phase. The host never stalls Android's lockscreen clock to manufacture a better relative result. Missing/stale content on an otherwise eligible trial is a miss.
3. On unlock, credentials, shade, occlusion or other restriction, the component owning the same frame excludes FULL from the first restricted composition, including transitions where the outgoing lockscreen is still drawn. Cancel/relock requires a newly eligible host decision. Establish coverage of separately composed occluding layers; a top-level SystemUI window identity or a composable mounted in a shared scene is insufficient. The host and the accessibility route must never simultaneously own a visible financial ORB. The relevant integration boundary is actual OEM SystemUI/keyguard composition and withdrawal, not simply assigning the APK a privileged permission.
4. First discriminating system test after a host is supplied: with a current distinctive revision already acknowledged, suspend the app process, then capture the first eligible host composition, first restrictive composition, and optical frames on the same display. Require canonical ORB in the former, no outgoing FULL in the latter, normal lockscreen timing, current revision through rapid relock, and first true motion without a jump. Exercise one missing/stale revision, a policy change and process/host loss. No release assertion from a mock or emulator counter.

**Acceptance.** Use maximum per trial, inclusive <=10 ms. Measure physical wake stimulus to first correct visible ORB pixel, first visible eligible ordinary lockscreen frame to that pixel, and first visible unlock/restrictive transition to first confirmed absence with last-visible bracket. Record first distinct motion separately. Use an external common-timed stimulus where required, calibrated high-speed optical frames or suitable sensors, matched scanline or scanout correction, and uncertainty. Upper bound <=10 passes that trial, lower bound >10 fails, straddling/missing endpoints are indeterminate. A delayed frame at 60 Hz costs about 16.67 ms; this is not a 16.67 ms minimum for two elements already in the same composition. A platform host could remove additional app/display frames relative to keyguard. Actual panel wake and physical scanout still bound stimulus-to-pixel latency. Do not substitute an internal 10 ms timer or a relative-to-lockscreen result for the physical wake result.

**Disposition for the coding agent.** R27 is delivered, physically rejected for wake and withdrawal, quantitative R27 phone endpoints unmeasured. Do not repeat the R27 optimization/build or silently initiate an OEM/ROM migration. There is no verified deployable system host in the Fluvi repo. Authorizing a reference platform prototype would permit empirical same-frame testing for that platform; shipping on ordinary unmodified devices still needs a distribution/integration contract. For the current simultaneous requirements, R28 is BLOCKED BY PLATFORM CONTRACT. This entry is a reviewer decision, not a new app release. No R28 application code, tests or APK were generated. Retain the public, verified APK delivery rule for actual future Android implementation handoffs.

## 8. CURRENT SOURCE FACTS

Fluvi's lib/app/platform/dashboard_keyguard_material_bridge.dart exports committed tuning and scoped material state. MainActivity.kt receives sceneTarget/publishProfile. Under android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen/, material/KeyguardMaterialProfile.kt and FluviKeyguardMaterialStore.publish/redact validate and store a revisioned profile. FluviKeyguardCardSettings.update/patchLayout affect disclosure, focus and geometry. Flutter's publisher counter resets per engine; visualKey excludes phase. Layout revision and focus generation are independent. observeCoreRevision in runtime/FluviLockScreenCard.kt can depend on the separate notification setting. A widget or service registry alone cannot own the new publisher.

material/KeyguardOrbSurfaceMaterial.kt provides the canonical painter, circle, static gradient, hardware poster and independent phases. KeyguardHeaderMaterialView.kt contains the canonical shader/configuration and KeyguardMaterialScene.timeAt/anchoredAt. The fixed shader generator in android/app/build.gradle.kts consumes shaders/dashboard_header_field.frag (source SHA-256 6be3e84d3e3ae6bffde549171b7319524768d67dbab1d55b74d565a4c76d4e7f), schema 1, ABI 6, adapter 9, 18 effects × plain/portal. The old DIRECT presenter may revoke FULL posters at seal. Keep the app's old render stack off the new host route.

At the AOSP pin, packages/SystemUI/compose/features/src/com/android/systemui/keyguard/ui/composable/LockscreenScene.kt delegates to LockscreenContent.kt; its selected blueprint calls DefaultBlueprint.kt in the blueprint subdirectory, where an existing Box contains topAreaSection.DefaultClockLayout. packages/SystemUI/compose/scene/src/com/android/compose/animation/scene/SceneTransitionLayout.kt exposes the outer ContentScope.layoutState, including active transitions and overlays. The clock also uses nested layout state; capture the outer one. SceneInteractor mirrors transition state asynchronously. LockscreenContentViewModel.isContentVisible defaults true, and KeyguardState.mapToSceneContainerContent collapses OFF/AOD/OCCLUDED/ALTERNATE_BOUNCER and LOCKSCREEN into the same scene key. None of those single values proves ordinary FULL eligibility.

## 9. PROVEN / UNPROVEN / MISSING EVIDENCE

PROVEN: a ready poster can be cheap once authorized, the current app decides too late in recorded phone trials, and the sample AOSP implementation owns an actual lockscreen draw site. UNPROVEN: first-frame inclusion, first restrictive-frame absence, matching visual/animation, and <=10 ms optical performance on any new build. MISSING: a patched booted R29 image, a physical device running this reference, cross-OEM host contracts and end-to-end R29 traces. The owner has requested this reference design and handoff; system-source availability permits implementing and testing it on the reference target. An unmodified phone has a different host.

## 10. ROOT-CAUSE CHOICE / FALSIFICATION

Move display ownership into the Android component that draws the ordinary lockscreen. Fluvi publishes the canonical parameters when state changes. SystemUI pre-renders and retains the correct first image plus a ready continuation before wake. The first eligible traversal only reads a local immutable ready slot and draws it beside the clock. The first restrictive traversal skips the old slot, even if the clock is still animating out. This is falsified for a trial if the first eligible frame lacks the matching FULL, a restricted frame carries the old image, the clock was delayed to make the images coincide, or steady wake/exit needs to wake Fluvi. Physical stimulus→pixel remains limited by actual panel wake.

## 11. IMPLEMENTATION SCOPE

One bounded reference integration using the real signed Fluvi producer, a platform-built SystemUI consumer, and the actual default lockscreen clock root. The userdebug prototype uses an explicitly enrolled disposable test user with reproducible demo transactions, ordinary ORB/orbOnly and known current projection. Exercise current animated material and the static/reduced-motion fallback. Fail closed on unknown revisions, non-default display/user/blueprint, missing host inputs or unsupported form factors. These misses remain in the panel/coverage report. Existing home widget, dashboard, signing key and package identity remain compatible. A stock device cannot activate the privileged renderer. A stand-alone test view, live wallpaper, accessibility overlay, privileged permission alone or mock SystemUI APK cannot be delivered as the integrated result.

## 13. RED TESTS AND CONTROL CONDITIONS

Before expensive platform work retain three distinguishing controls. (1) Stock R27 or unpatched reference image has no SystemUI ORB after disabling the accessibility presentation. (2) Deliberately paint the **synthetic** demo marker one host frame late in a test-only renderer; the first-frame scorer must fail. (3) Keep a synthetic old frame for one exit traversal; the withdrawal scorer must fail. Use a wrong revision/palette and partial old ORB as negative image controls. The safe compiled shipping path must never expose a deliberately stale image. Absent private data, absent clock, loading/spinner, black surface and neutral placeholder are not substitutes for the positive. Combine (a) inset-aware full-screen evidence with a before/after reference and (b) host revision/frame metadata. Keep the real installed Fluvi publisher and platform integration distinguishable from deterministic unit fixtures.

## 14. EXACT IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT

**A. Build the source pair.** Add a small producer package under .../lockscreen/host/, an explicitly versioned shared data contract under platform/aosp16/contract/, and a pinned, reviewable frameworks/base patch under platform/aosp16/patches/. Add stage/verify scripts scoped to that reference which check the upstream SHA, apply only the listed patch to a clean worktree, stage fixed renderer sources/assets, and produce parent/tree/file digests. No edits to a user's Android installation. Carry the actual SystemUI service, renderer, eligibility logic, DI/lifecycle, blueprint edit, Soong inputs and host tests in the deliverable. A description or patch of only the clock Composable is insufficient.

**B. Publish on change, not wake.** Add an internal publisher driven after validated FluviKeyguardMaterialStore.publish plus explicit settings, layout, projection and redaction changes. Derive authority from validated projection/target, independent of the accessibility service or notification setting. Subscribe to relevant core revision changes while enrolled. If source revisions no longer match, revoke eligibility immediately and wait for an authoritative fresh projection; never promote a stale profile because it is in preferences. Publish schema version, session, sequence, visual/data/focus/layout/privacy revisions, checked source period/validity boundary, display density/dimensions/placement, disclosure class and independently specified elapsed/base/background/interior phase plus existing immutable material parameters. Preserve current static, motion, alpha, stops and portal treatment. A legitimate neutral/unsupported state is represented explicitly. Geometry conversion uses the existing inset-safe travel fractions for the 64 dp ORB, not raw camera pixels. No balances, text, raw database rows, shader source, actions or arbitrary dimensions in IPC. A bounded descriptor is sufficient. SystemUI generates its own poster once from these parameters.

**C. Transport, freshness and lifetime.** Add an explicit Binder endpoint to platform SystemUI for the debuggable reference product, inert by default, and a narrow app client. App verifies the expected explicit installed system component, reference platform trust and version before supplying a descriptor. Each incoming Binder call verifies the calling UID actually owns the pinned com.fluvi.app signed with the established certificate, the supported Android user and current enrollment; reject spoofed parcel identities, isolated/other users and ambiguous shared publisher UIDs. SystemUI uses android.uid.systemui at this pin; do not hardcode UID 1000. App validates the trusted host identity on callbacks. Validate payload lengths/counts, finite numeric ranges, supported enum and current material schema at ingress. Cap the entire typed descriptor (32 KiB upper bound), rate-coalesce normal replacements, process restrictive invalidation immediately. No application-supplied executable shader/URI/remote view. Test missing/spoofed host on stock.

Host creates a fresh session token after enrollment/restart. PREPARE and INVALIDATE carry monotonic sequence within this session. Acknowledge actual worker completion of the generation after main/draw owner adoption, never plain receipt. If a generation is no longer current at either point, release it. A replacement that invalidates prior visual/data/policy immediately hides the old entry until the correct replacement is ready. For the test input use an explicitly enrolled demo snapshot with a known validity boundary. Stop serving it on policy tightening, scope expiry/day/clock/timezone change, package removal/replace, display/configuration change, user switch or host reset. In controlled mutable tests start a revoke barrier before accepting a restrictive edit into the enrolled snapshot; publish only the committed replacement. Use an asynchronous acknowledgement, no blocking on app or SystemUI main. If unsignalled external writes cannot be covered, mark that live-data mode unqualified and keep real balances outside the reference experiment. A clean client detach may leave an already acknowledged, immutable, still-valid demo revision available; app death must not resurrect in-flight work. A fresh session cannot use an old nonce/revision. No disk restoration of FULL in SystemUI after restart. The host must remain able to hide without contacting Fluvi.

**D. Exactly one visible owner.** Use a durable opt-in setting for the reference pairing and epoch, separate from ordinary keyguard requested settings. Start enrollment while the ORB is withdrawn. Persist app-side suppression of both DIRECT and legacy/stock overlay publication before allowing the platform owner; invalidate pending acquisitions/grants and drain the old native/window owner. Recheck suppression at source admission and the actual final show/submit boundary; it survives app/service restart and late callbacks. Host grants ownership only after this epoch's affirmative quiescence; when exiting, host first revokes/withdraws and acknowledges empty, then the app may explicitly resume its original route. On ambiguity both remain withdrawn. No automatic dual fallback on a Binder death. Conformance setup on disposable Cuttlefish additionally disables the Fluvi accessibility service and proves its absence during the measured system-only case. On a fresh stock phone without the enrolled host, continue existing stock behavior and export HOST_UNAVAILABLE; never present this as a fix for the rejected R27 stock path. Preserve installer data; only the explicitly paired test user changes ownership.

**E. Ready host image and motion.** Reuse the pure material decode/validation, shader configuration, static gradient, phase math and drawing portions of KeyguardMaterialProfile, KeyguardHeaderShader, KeyguardMaterialScene and KeyguardOrbSurfacePainter; isolate renderer-only code from preferences, Android services, app BuildConfig, Flutter and View hierarchy. Use a single reviewable canonical source or deterministic verified staging from that source in the reference build. Stage only known generated effects/assets with the generator's own hash convention; pin generator, metadata, ABI and asset digests in the platform artifact. Independent mutable painter instances for independent threads. On semantic revision/configuration change only, in the host worker, validate/copy inputs, construct/prepare program and a host-owned immutable first picture of the actual bounded dimensions at t0. Ensure it can be sampled by the host hardware canvas before reporting READY. Track what the device actually warmed: neither a constructed RuntimeShader nor prepareToDraw alone proves a GPU fence or perpetual residency. Capture the real first host draw, texture/queue cost and fence evidence where available. No speculative private surface visible before the scene permits it.

Store one ready entry plus one coalesced/in-flight replacement; publish immutable references atomically. Close/release stale work and resources only when prior consumers/GPU use permit; bound memory as a function of actual dimensions, record peak. Keep a prepared, separately owned host-side live renderer. At the first eligible draw select the last ready matching revision and draw the poster. Start the visible phase clock from the presented/selected first phase; subsequent visible draws use canonical elapsed/base/background/interior phase increments, independent of the Fluvi process. No shader parse/compile, disk, Binder, new window, new financial read or poster construction is permitted in the first draw or exit decision. Offscreen state is retained without animating. On memory pressure evict safely and mark the entry not ready; report misses honestly.

**F. Compose the actual lockscreen frame.** In the default blueprint keep the outside ContentScope.layoutState before entering any nested clock layout. At LockscreenContent.Content, after its existing empty-content guard and blueprint selection, wrap the supported default blueprint content in a full-root Box, preserving its original constraints, modifier application and sysuiResTag. Keep the existing blueprint as the measuring child and insert a non-measuring matchParentSize draw child for the ORB below the existing NotificationLockscreenScrim. Apply unchanged behavior to other blueprint paths. Do not index the ORB as a direct child of the DefaultBlueprint custom Layout or constrain the configured screen position to the small clock Box. Feed explicit clock traversal identity from the existing default clock path for comparison, without making the clock wait for it. Preserve z-order, FOD, UDFPS, semantics, no hit targets, and all clock/notification layout branches; test actual text/controls and insets against the unmodified root. Use immutable host snapshot and current draw-time eligibility. Required affirmative inputs are actual selected ordinary lockscreen, default user/display/blueprint, proper visible geometry, eligible privacy policy, current ready revision, no dismiss/going-away, occlusion, dream, doze/AOD, credential/bouncer or shade/QS overlay. Read outer layout transition/overlay state used by this traversal; integrate a restrictive latch at the *start* of actual exit/credential/shade/occlusion transitions, invalidate the render node immediately, and exclude the outgoing ORB even while its parent lockscreen remains on screen. Use the outer SceneTransitionLayoutState.currentTransitions/currentOverlays including interruptions, together with KeyguardInteractor.isDozing/isDreaming/isKeyguardOccluded/isKeyguardGoingAway and ShadeInteractor.shadeExpansion/isShadeAnyExpanded as restrictive inputs. Missing/unknown initial observations deny FULL; use one draw-consistent immutable policy sample. Do not infer affirmative permission from a default false value. Combine these inputs with trusted keyguard/power/WM state; KeyguardTransitionRepositoryImpl.startTransition supplies early restrictive transition identity. Reset restrictive latches only for a new affirmatively eligible state. Async SceneInteractor.currentScene, currentKeyguardState and isContentVisible are insufficient by themselves. If an in-flight incoming transition can visibly contain nonordinary content, leave the ORB absent and grade the true first eligible lockscreen image externally; never move the scoring origin to the next idle scene. First implementation is intentionally fail-closed for unsupported/ambiguous combinations.

A separate surface/window can change the visible composition without a matching keyguard subtree traversal. Exercise an actual occluding activity, not just a boolean. If a separately composed restriction cannot be joined at the same frame boundary, retain failing evidence, keep the reference demo-only, and report that configuration UNQUALIFIED. Do not promote the lab design to production or invent a WM exclusion exemption. Never synchronize system clock presentation to ORB readiness.

**G. Observability.** Emit a bounded versioned record from both components: source/host build IDs, fallback/enrolled owner, nonce fingerprint, generation/revisions, publish/accept/revoke/ready, first clock/ORB traversal, first motion, restrictive traversal and final absence. Include frame/vsync id when supported, clock source and alignment uncertainty; field absence is explicit. Record counters for draw on wrong revision, missed first frame, duplicated owner and app IPC/disk/compile during wake. Keep private content, shader uniforms and financial values out of logs. Heavy trace capture is opt-in. Add the host status/revisions to existing diagnostic export without displacing the critical app receipts or exceeding 32 KiB. A host CPU record cannot declare pixels presented.

## 15. PERFORMANCE AND PHYSICAL ACCEPTANCE

Score three independent maxima <=10 ms: physical wake stimulus to first correct FULL pixel; first visible eligible ordinary lockscreen frame to that same pixel; first visible unlock/restrictive transition to first confirmed absence (bracket last visible and first absent). Preserve milliseconds and number of display frames. Report first distinct motion separately. Upper bound <=10 passes that trial, lower bound >10 fails, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. An eligible blank/missing/stale image does not pass. Compare normal clock appearance against unmodified or paired host-off controls; no deliberate wait for READY. Cover cold/no prepared resource, prepared warm, and fast unlock/relock separately. Reference warm proof: ACK current image, disconnect and stop the app process without changing package, user or session; record absence before/after wake and no rebind or process start. Prefer normal non-force-stop process kill after unbinding while app is backgrounded, verify PID absence; distinguish this from package force-stop/removal which may deliberately revoke eligibility.

On a bootable reference, predeclare A/B/B/A, two ordinary warm wakes per block, A = R27 overlay on same image with host off, B = R29 paired host only. Include a separate paired host-off reference for first clock and the killed-app control. Reuse all compatible A/B samples, keep outliers and failed set-ups. Upper/lower optical bounds need high-speed external camera or sensors, calibrated scanout/settings, common physical wake marker and same-scanline reference or measured correction. Cuttlefish compositor evidence can establish common system frames and functional absence; optical endpoints on a handset remain PENDING until the owner tests a physically compatible integrated system. Do not ask the owner to flash anything as part of this job.

## 16. IMPLEMENTATION ORDER / HANDLING FAILURES

Pin the two sources, write protocol/reducer/ownership RED tests, implement producer and host store, canonical renderer/preparation and golden parity, then exact SystemUI patch plus scene tests, then real composed-image tests and qualified artifact delivery. Start source work and cheap lanes even if a full-platform builder is unavailable. Run independent APK packaging, source verification and testable host contract work to completion. Keep each first failure. One targeted rerun per mechanically corrected boundary with new evidence; assess all observed failures before escalation. If a frame authority or data-freshness contract is disproved, retain exact source/log/frames and refer that design decision to the reviewer, without changing disclosure rules.

### 14. Implementation contract

1. **App publisher.** Add one process-scoped coordinator in lockscreen/host, created from the real enrollment/diagnostic entry and reached by accepted material/settings changes. Add a scoped read that captures the current core revision, category, limits and totals for the existing target within one Room read transaction on the same database. Put the narrow read operation inside android/fluvi-core, where FluviCore owns the private database, and return only a revisioned projection to FluviLockScreenCardCoordinator. Reuse existing scope/limit calculations and canonical color mapping. Pass its provenance and focus/layout/privacy snapshot through sceneTarget.toMap and the actual Dart frame producer. Bind the material generation to the visual source at derivation. Where an existing dashboard frame has no matching scoped evidence, mark it unavailable. For the reference positive, seed a supported Budget/category color-scale projection derived from the returned category color and remaining percent. Keep Mind or any unsupported/stale projection neutral or absent. Preserve other existing stock modes. Use a single non-reused host sequence per session. Reject stale native publisher epoch and mismatched target/visual/current revisions. Use background, enrollment-scoped observation independent of accessibility and notification state. Route restrictive edits via an asynchronous revoke-before-accept barrier on the reference snapshot. Handle time validity, process death and missing or unsignalled writes as in R29 §14. Keep FULL eligible after clean detach only for the already adopted, still-valid immutable demo.

2. **Old owner and Binder handover.** Provide durable R29Ownership.Store with atomic suppression/epoch writes and an in-memory gate visible on all display lanes. Reserve a handover epoch before draining. Coordinate with reserveR18WakeBeforeMain, refreshR18RouteOnMain, applyResolvedPresentation and KeyguardCardWindow.showOrUpdate (attach and retained visibility). On the DIRECT output lane serialize/check generation at KeyguardOrbDirectOutput.reveal's final visibility-apply boundary. If an earlier transaction crossed already, wait for its ordered hide/unparent and release. Always allow revoke/withdraw. Join onR18Drained, window removal and outstanding outputs for that epoch before oldOwnerDrained. Reference loss or invalid persistence stays fail-closed after restart. Fresh stock with no paired host continues normally. Use the existing OWNERSHIP opcode and EMPTY callback. Negotiate matching protocol version with the paired host, carry epoch, nonce, revoke sequence and actual empty-frame receipt. Anchor the receipt at the SystemUI composition root even when the ORB subtree has been removed. Reject mismatched and replayed receipts. Call hostConfirmedEmpty only after a matching receipt verified again on the current app coordinator. Leaving while disconnected stays suppressed until authenticated reconciliation confirms the host is empty. Bind/unbind/death notifications must also match their connection generation. Keep signer, UID, package, user, length and finite-input checks. Stock final display remains allowed only by its original authorization policy.

3. **Resident slot.** Worker validates, renders and submits the prepared candidate. Pass completion through workerFinished. Main/draw owner rechecks epoch, nonce, sequence, validity and disposition, adopts the slot, registers its active display owner and only then acknowledges READY to the current session. Serialize final receipt delivery with invalidation. Distinguish explicit clean DETACH from unexpected callback Binder death: clear pending and unacknowledged output on both, reset on an unexpected death, and identity-check and unlink the matching death recipient when clean detach has completed. A delayed death from an old connection cannot revoke a new one. Reject worker completions after reset, unclean disconnect or disposal. Schedule clock/validity invalidation even for a static image. Avoid awaitForever blocking the sole worker. Use the off-main finite fence wait API, e.g. SyncFence.await(Duration.ofSeconds(1)) as a preparation failure bound only. Require a successful render status and a valid fence with exclusive lifetime across the wait; Android treats an invalid fence as already signalled. See [Android SyncFence](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/hardware/SyncFence). On timeout mark not ready; retain at most one quarantined GPU job, with a release-only watcher for its original fence/owner and no additional allocations until the safe release. Preserve the completion path for a late valid signal; invalid or missing release proof leaves that resource quarantined until teardown. Record timeout/miss, never allow it to authorize a frame. Keep one current slot, one in-flight candidate and one coalesced descriptor. Release retired references only when their consumers/GPU have finished.

4. **Platform draw and exclusion.** Complete the reviewable patch and deterministic staging against the pinned frameworks/base. In packages/SystemUI/compose/features/src/com/android/systemui/keyguard/ui/composable/LockscreenContent.kt keep isContentVisible's empty layout, outer ContentScope.layoutState, the existing blueprint selection, clock sizing/constraints and keyguard_root_view tag. For the supported default blueprint only, keep the original content as the measuring child of a full-root Box, then a passive matchParentSize drawing child below NotificationLockscreenScrim. ### 14. Implementation contract

1. In readSystemWindows reuse the physical firstAcquisition selection. On API 35 pair R18_INITIAL_HYBRID with an optional immutable original-opening identity. Require openingHandoff's current A handle, virgin DIRECT reservation/route/preparation via KeyguardR27VirginDirectPolicy.matches, current request/freshness and detached/no proof/no grant. Revalidate once on exact accepted window selection after the root returns. Do not acquire the queue lock per child. A later state change uses existing per-node authority/cancellation and final proof checks.
2. On the milestone run a fixture through the real reader and queue. Establish virgin unpublished DIRECT A→B, clean attributable SystemUI root, and an inventory with remaining children. ### 14. Implementation contract

1. Add one runtime follow-on handle to KeyguardOpeningInspectionHandoff for the exact original reservation, route revision, session/wake and B request/authority. Set B's read-start scene under queueLock immediately before physical windows acquisition. Record post-start invalidations and match a post-start real INSPECT offer with its actual pending occupant, ingress ID, current scene and default display. The candidate eligibility is independent of diagnostics. The ambiguous framework event in this capture can invalidate B and request a fresh read. It supplies no SystemUI identity, FULL proof or permission to discard a restriction. Require the independent physical SystemUI inventory below. Exact own, foreign-app origin, missing display, synthetic/no matching offer, wrong/future state, and inherited freshness debt cannot transfer.
2. Give B only a read-only hint and one claim callback on the existing returned-node/pre-next-child path. Reuse the baseline classifier, cleanOpeningInventory, strict attribution, freshness checks and exact not-yet-visible DIRECT guards. Require an accepted default-display SystemUI root, exact own-window handling, no missing/truncated node or disqualifier in the consumed prefix, and work still remaining. Do not move the opportunity before root identity, issue an extra Binder call or alter any prefetch flags. Recheck scope and cancel stale hints before a new claim. Separate A's historical incomplete-null-child path from B's clean-only path.
3. At claim under queueLock, require active==B, actual pending==the exact latest C, newer scene distinct from B read-start, matched request/ingress, current authority/route/reservation, satisfied freshness obligation, no preceding ordered apply, no retained proof, no paint/grant/visible/touchable or recovery state. Use handoffOpening(B,C) and consume the follow-on exactly once. Return the typed Yielded result, close original B's post-claim observation as YIELDED_TO_C, and recycle B's already acquired objects normally. Skip completed-read publication for this partial B. C starts one complete fresh service read. No C→D transfer. Further invalidations continue through the baseline path.
4. Fix the specific cancellation gap in processInspectionQueue.finally: always use exact ownership checks. During B unwind check the recorded transfer pair for that B even if promotedOwner still points to B and abandonSessionIfActive(B) returned false. Never clear a different session or a new successor from an old A cleanup. No queue lock around node acquisition, recycling, system calls, tests or tracing. Each terminal path closes or clears only its own handle.
5. Extend compact evidence keyed by capture/session/wake/A/B/reservation. Include B start scene, newer offer time/ID/origin/scene, actual C and displacement, in-flight call end where observed, first usable checkpoint or rejection, number of B calls after offer, transfer/unwind, C start/end, ultimate proof and winner, reveal/first-post/withdrawal timestamps. Keep A's historical post-claim record intact. Preserve app uptime and paired monotonic nanoseconds in their own domains. Capture OFF and capture rotation must not change which request runs. Do not retain platform node or financial payload. At the existing DIRECT fallback site distinguish the failing existing input predicate with scalar evidence available at decision time; leave the outcome unchanged and avoid recomputing a decision after the owner has changed.

Publish a current, versioned initial image and phase parameters on data/config/policy change. Acknowledge resources before wake. Its production publisher wiring, exclusive handover, actual keyguard frame integration and restrictive/empty receipt are unfinished (see platform/aosp16/README.md and docs/R29_1_RESIDENT_SYSTEMUI_CHECKPOINT_2026-11-23.md). The reference needs a compatible system image. Public AppWidget hosting depends on the device and trigger and does not establish ordinary-wake placement or a universal 10 ms guarantee. No ROM migration or R32 application build is being initiated. Public references: https://android-developers.googleblog.com/2025/03/widgets-on-lock-screen-faq.html and https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/KeyguardManager#isKeyguardLocked().
