Under android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen, FluviKeyguardCardService.invalidateR19Scene and KeyguardFirstAuthorizedOrb.requireRead order new demand. inspectSurface takes the scene serial before readSystemWindows, acquires a full window inventory and ID tree, classifies it and samples system state. readInspection records completion; decisive restriction can seal on the reader before Main. processInspectionQueue supports one physical reader and an ordered preceding Main apply. Existing R12 read-ahead accepts particular detached negatives. R25 completed-positive optimization deliberately bypasses DIRECT (DIRECT_ORDERED). On other DIRECT completed positives the worker awaits Main before serving the next pending request. A known-obsolete positive can still require Main-side exclusion checks, own-window identity bookkeeping or a downgrade. Simply dropping applyInspection or flipping the R25 route flag would violate ownership.

On the host side, R29PublisherSnapshot.create already validates projection, layout, privacy and core revisions. R29OwnershipStore is durable. R29ResidentStore.enqueue already adopts prepared output on Main and handles expiry. R29HostRenderer already has finite preparation and quarantine. The remaining gaps are the real producer, suppression/drain at all display gates, real keyguard drawing, restrictive-frame invalidation and ownership exit receipt. R29HostClient ignores CALLBACK_EMPTY; FluviOrbHostService handles TRANSACTION_OWNERSHIP by invalidating the store. R29PreparedOrb.draw has no ordinary keyguard composition caller. The platform patch registers build/service bootstrap only. Do not reimplement the completed pieces.

### 14. Implementation contract

**S — ordinary host, single reader.** Add a small typed plan for a completed predecessor in the service's processInspectionQueue, e.g. StockDetachedNegative or ObsoleteDirectPositive, held with immutable reservation, read-ahead state revision, complete authority, freshness, read scene, exact requests and pending proof obligation. Reuse the existing queue and preceding/active/pending ownership. A fresh visible grant still has one owner. Do not instantiate a second reader, expand R31 mid-walk transfers, suppress accessibility events, fabricate a newer request, park a DIRECT positive in R25, or redeem a previously captured FULL decision.

1. At the existing completed-read scheduling decision under queueLock, retain R12's current predicate unchanged. For S additionally require: active A equals completed A, no preceding owner, actual pending B is newer, genuine same-wake framework ingress, same current service/visibility/wake/interaction/attach authority; same route revision and reserved hidden DIRECT owner with purpose EMPTY_AWAITING_DISCLOSURE; no retained/consumed proof, pending grant/input/paint/visible/recovery, or queued publication. Capture immutable scalar state on its owning thread if a predicate now lives on Main; never access Views or mutable Main fields on Worker. OFF/unknown state cannot qualify. A must be complete FULL/MAIN_CONFIRMED, current system eligibility in its read, no truncation/stale/ambiguous-own evidence. Both requests share established freshness revision, no unserved clear, and the *actual read scene differs from current scene*. A newer ID or a diagnostic rejection string alone is insufficient. Reserve B atomically via reserveSuccessor. Do not clear required reads or acknowledge freshness here. Other cases take the exact baseline route.
2. On the single worker start physical B immediately, in parallel only with ordered Main disposal of completed A. Preserve existing R12 logic in its own arm. Mark A in the immutable plan as irrevocably forbidden to disclose. Apply A's still-relevant safety/negative checks, fresh system admission, own-window and diagnostic/reconciliation side effects in their normal order. At the first point any positive behavior could be scheduled, forbid that behavior for A, including DIRECT preparation, fallback display, stock publication, recovery, input and callbacks. Do not hide merely because A was a stale positive. Early system exclusions still win. If a guard change makes the paired path inapplicable, dispose/reconcile under current authority; never replay A normally as a fresh positive. Route changes or concurrent hides cannot use an old plan to remove a new owner.
3. B obtains its own before/after system samples, physical inventory, scene stamp, complete classification, and normal fresh proof. Restrictive signals/marker/worker seal remain immediate. Positive publication must wait until A's exact ordered disposal completed and must revalidate the exact still-current reservation/route/snapshot, authority, request/read order, scene, proof, input and latest required read. A newer C disqualifies B according to baseline. A cannot authorize B. In finally release preceding by exact A and current B, preserve any newer pending, handle exceptions, dispatcher cancellation and service teardown without stranding the queue. Place pairing before r25CompleteLocked in processInspectionQueue. Keep beforeRead/establishFreshness, readCompleted, readSystemWindows.onDecisiveSystemMarker and sealR18 under their present owners. Use a distinct typed argument through applyCompletedInspection into applyInspection to keep the predecessor restriction-only; do not treat a historical operand as a live view or fresh signal. Implement the single-reader sequence as follows:

        reserve exact (A, B) under queueLock
        dispatch ordered, restriction-capable A to Main
        read B on the existing physical reader; keep any complete positive unpublished
        await A disposal outside all locks; release preceding for A only
        on exact revalidation, use B's normal ordered Main path once
        otherwise reject B and preserve/reacquire current pending demand
        on every cancellation release only this pair and reconcile the surviving owner

In particular A's Main callback must service the current gate if unlock arrived; do not copy the existing speculative-negative branch unchanged if its early readAheadStillCurrent rejection would discard that obligation. If B was still the active request when a later C arrived, B cannot be renamed to C. On nested read-ahead, the queue rejects another reservation while preceding is non-null. No Android/IPC, allocation-heavy diagnostics, wait or thread join under queueLock. Publish a bounded capture-only row with A/B/C ids, scenes, reserve, physical read start/end, A Main enter/exit/disposition, B proof/grant/withdraw and real backend. Keep scheduling independent of capture OFF/LIGHT/FULL. Use scalar counters and the current critical-record budget.

## 8. Current source facts

In stock, FluviKeyguardCardService.reserveR18WakeBeforeMain/advanceR19First join current disclosure proof, output, hidden bind and paint. KeyguardOrbR18Presenter.seal calls worker.revoke(discardFull=true). KeyguardOrbSurfaceWorker removes FULL posters on that path and skips retirement poster generation. Its lookup includes visual key, dimensions, density, disclosure and four phase/time components. KeyguardOrbDirectProgramWarmup indexes effect/portal and builds a program with no uniforms, image or pixel submission. So changing a cache flag alone either saves a short worker interval or risks an outdated/private frame. It cannot create the earlier authorization or force SystemUI to include an app layer in the clock frame.

In the reference, R29HostRenderer.prepare already creates the actual poster, separately prepares the live painter, and adopts only after its bounded GPU check. R29PreparedOrb.draw already draws the poster first. There is no production call from the pinned keyguard root. The platform patch touches Android.bp and the SystemUI manifest; it does not patch LockscreenContent. R29HostClient discards CALLBACK_EMPTY. The stock APK cannot install those system components.

## 10. Root cause / falsification

For the demonstrated software delay, the decisive dependency is late display authority: the first FULL frame waits for an asynchronous post-wake observation on an owner outside the keyguard composition. In attempt 1 even first-frame paint authority and reveal authority diverged. The relevant test holds the producer asleep after a clean acknowledged publish: the ordinary clock must still appear on time with the right ORB in its first eligible frame. Any wake-time app read, IPC, decode, substitute color, or first correct frame after that frame falsifies the structural change. No new queue-hop experiment.

## 11. Scope lock

Stock operating systems without a verified integration retain their actual capabilities; their route cannot be relabeled FIRST_FRAME. Public keyguard AppWidget placement and triggers depend on the host. A lockscreen wallpaper replaces a user surface and cannot certify our specific disclosure rules. Neither is a drop-in universal equivalent. No new accessibility privileges, stale-proof reuse, launcher widget edits, wallpaper replacement, notification disguise or alteration of ordinary keyguard behavior. The proposed platform implementation remains default-off in the established reference lane. Do not substitute it as a deliverable for a stock-only decision.

## 13. Required red / negative tests

H1: publish exact A1, then B, then A2 through real accepted app input; hold and deliver A1 last. Only A2 may be eligible. Change palette/data/period/geometry and privacy; cold, expired, malformed or unknown gives an empty slot. Cross-process stale source cannot silently keep FULL. H2: from visible stock and from queued native submit enter host enrollment, interrupt on each side of submit, then restart. Exactly one visual/input owner or safely none. H3: leave while visible/offscreen, delay old session's READY/EMPTY, restart or kill publisher; only a matching applied absence permits handback. Preserve distinct clean detach and unexpected death.

H4: on the real reference image, with a prepared demo revision and the app cleanly detached and suspended, observe first clock frame and correct cached ORB, at their actual bounds; the OFF control must still show the clock at the ordinary time. H5: shade/QS, PIN, actual foreign occluding window, unlock, interrupted relock with previously visible FULL. Examine the first restrictive presentation including retained transition surfaces. A known late-by-one-frame specimen and a partially visible old ORB must fail the scorer. H6: correct first poster phase, next distinct motion, static/reduced motion, low-memory drop and expiry; no detached ticker. Missing parent draw, positive exposure, unclassified pixels and failure to reach setup are different results. Keep trial IDs and all outcomes.

## 14. Implementation contract

1. Publication is triggered by accepted data/material/settings/layout/privacy/expiry changes while the phone is awake; initial preparation must already have finished before the tested lock/wake. Connect MainActivity's accepted publishProfile result and the authoritative sceneTarget/current revision to R29PublisherSnapshot.create and R29HostClient.publish. A finite-validity frozen demo projection suffices for the reference control; label it.

Revoke on mismatch, time/zone, switch or disconnect as the existing lifecycle requires. Keep expensive canonical painting, shader setup and GPU preparation off the draw thread. No disk content read on wake. Adopt outside external callback execution and keep stale-safe revalidation at receipt.
3. Supply a single scene-local draw decision: on an eligible ordinary keyguard traversal with known current identity and valid READY, draw that poster directly into the clock's composition. Otherwise omit the ORB from that traversal; leave the clock independent and count the miss. For animation, reuse the exact poster phase and existing live painter in subsequent eligible frames. Reset after exclusion. Pure pre-rendering cannot set permission to display financial data.
4. Feed restrictive scene/overlay/occlusion input before the frame that can expose an outgoing layer. At the pinned platform the implementation class KeyguardTransitionRepositoryImpl lives in src/com/android/systemui/keyguard/data/repository/KeyguardTransitionRepository.kt; its startTransition is a transition boundary, not by itself proof of all shade or WindowManager occlusion cases. Retire outgoing recorded content in the same transition. Disable the path for any unsupported ordering. If the PAIRED reference cannot supply synchronously ordered independent occlusion, return the specific missing contract without weakening FULL exclusion.
5. Integrate R29Ownership with existing app reservation, fallback/window and final native submit. Suppress first, capture every outstanding old-owner ticket, drain, then authenticate handover. Extend R29HostClient/FluviOrbHostService from invalidate-only leave to immutable epoch/sequence-matched empty receipt from an actually replaced/presented empty frame or confirmed destroyed visible layer. No ACK under lock, no timer-based transfer. Reference failure must never cause two owners. Machine-test the reverse handoff before enabling the real display node.
6. Put targeted diagnostics in those exact components in the same candidate: one bounded row per wake/restriction, route, session fingerprint, epoch/seq, ready-before-wake, ready/miss reason, eligible/clock/poster/first-motion/first-restrictive/empty frame IDs and clock domain; count wake-time producer/disk/IPC/compile calls. No values, pixels or identifiers from financial data in public evidence. Distinguish generated, adopted, submitted, composed and optically visible.

## 15. Performance gate

Owner's ceiling is 10 ms maximum, inclusive. Report separately physical wake stimulus → correct FULL; first eligible lockscreen clock → correct FULL; first restrictive frame → disappearance. Clock-relative zero extra frames is the design target. Do not count a delayed clock as success. At 60 Hz a missed frame is nominally 16.67 ms. Same frame can satisfy the relative target; neither frame ID nor renderer time certifies button-to-photon latency. Use a common-timed independent high-speed capture or equivalent calibrated sensors with screen scanout correction, reference points at matched scan positions and reported uncertainty. Score each trial with an interval: upper bound ≤10 passes, lower bound >10 fails, straddling is indeterminate. Report max, misses and every failed attempt separately. A finite sample cannot prove a universal bound. Cold unprimed and warm are separate; do not exclude cold/miss from an unconditional claim.

**Disposition: STOCK FIRST-FRAME CONTRACT UNAVAILABLE on the inspected route.** The requested product is an ordinarily installable APK on factory Android. The owner requires the configured FULL ORB to be ready before lock and visible in the first eligible clock frame even while the Fluvi process is suspended, with a maximum visible delay of 10 ms. A fast worker is not proof of that contract. The first precondition in the R33 handoff is unmet, so no R33 application implementation, APK build, app-only CI cycle or phone-test artifact was started. The existing R32 APK is not represented as an R33 repair. This is a finding about the checked integration and evidence, not a proof that every current or future OEM Android implementation lacks a suitable interface.

**Refs and source scope.** The fetched coordination branch `fix/orb-v4-latency-lockscreen` was `559b0b0b6cecfd627d28ab07f3e28b2b2dcef09d`, exactly the pinned R33 handoff; there were no subsequent commits on that branch at inspection. That commit adds only the 147-line journal entry. The phone-tested app branch `implement/r32-first-frame` remains `14e05315520ff3282348838804ff6e004c677d30`, parent `5b18235f261df24dcee06cf3050e3e20411612fa`. The separate, unfinished reference branch remains `e6df9043cb1a879d1f28a3128ee01a543cb8e59b`, parent `14e05315`. The coordination and app tips are different histories: the coordination journal tip is not the installed application SHA. No application source was modified in this check.

**The stock display boundary.** The manifest registers the opt-in accessibility service, and the window geometry uses `TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY` rather than a SystemUI-owned keyguard content node ([manifest](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/blob/14e05315520ff3282348838804ff6e004c677d30/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml#L58), [geometry](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/blob/14e05315520ff3282348838804ff6e004c677d30/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen/KeyguardCardGeometry.kt#L143), [window add](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/blob/14e05315520ff3282348838804ff6e004c677d30/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen/KeyguardCardWindow.kt#L669)). The wake path reserves an inspection; `advanceR19First` requires a current proof, matching authority and revisions, ready output, and a fresh SHOW_FULL system sample before the first paint is authorized ([reservation](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/blob/14e05315520ff3282348838804ff6e004c677d30/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen/FluviKeyguardCardService.kt#L526), [first authorization](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/blob/14e05315520ff3282348838804ff6e004c677d30/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen/FluviKeyguardCardService.kt#L830)). These checks protect current disclosure and must not be bypassed to report a faster opening. They also do not supply the factory SystemUI with a pre-authorized, current ORB to include in its first clock frame while Fluvi cannot execute.

`KeyguardOrbDirectProgramWarmup` prepares an effect/portal program, not a ready-to-display image ([warmup](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/blob/14e05315520ff3282348838804ff6e004c677d30/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen/material/KeyguardOrbDirectProgramWarmup.kt#L37)). On the applicable seal path the presenter revokes the target with `discardFull=true`; the worker removes FULL posters and does not create a retirement poster in that case ([presenter](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/blob/14e05315520ff3282348838804ff6e004c677d30/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen/material/KeyguardOrbR18Presenter.kt#L260), [worker](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/blob/14e05315520ff3282348838804ff6e004c677d30/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen/material/KeyguardOrbSurfaceWorker.kt#L514)). Preserving a bitmap or shortening a worker alone would not supply the missing current disclosure authority or a first-clock-frame composition hook.

**What is missing from the separate reference.** The [reference README](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/blob/e6df9043cb1a879d1f28a3128ee01a543cb8e59b/platform/aosp16/README.md) explicitly describes an incomplete, disabled checkpoint. Its renderer can prepare a poster and `R29PreparedOrb.draw` can draw that poster, but the [bootstrap patch](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/blob/e6df9043cb1a879d1f28a3128ee01a543cb8e59b/platform/aosp16/patches/0001-r29-host-bootstrap-WIP.patch) changes only SystemUI build assets and manifest registration. The pinned AOSP `LockscreenContent.kt` at `android-16.0.0_r1` / `99b01a65cc4c104933788b3143285ab6bae65827` contains no ORB draw hook. A source search at `14e05315` found `R29HostClient` and `R29Ownership` class definitions but no production constructor call or `R29PublisherSnapshot.create` call. The [client](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/blob/e6df9043cb1a879d1f28a3128ee01a543cb8e59b/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen/host/R29HostClient.kt#L135) ignores `CALLBACK_EMPTY` and the [host](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/blob/e6df9043cb1a879d1f28a3128ee01a543cb8e59b/platform/aosp16/systemui/src/com/android/systemui/keyguard/fluvi/FluviOrbHostService.kt#L182) invalidates rather than acknowledging a genuinely empty composed frame. Publisher-to-host delivery, the real scene draw, current restriction/occlusion ordering and exclusive owner/empty-frame handover are therefore missing; even this separate reference is not a finished or verified first-frame solution. Installing an ordinary APK does not install its SystemUI patch.

The missing product integration is an available and authorized **stock-device display owner/interface** which can hold the correct current prepared ORB independently of the app process, incorporate it into the eligible lockscreen clock composition, and exclude it for the first restricted/unlock frame. No such integration was found on the specified coordination branch or in the checked app/reference sources. ### 8. Private cache before lock

Prepare the actual configured transparent image of the orb on a worker at accepted profile/data/settings changes, service initialisation and legitimate idle invalidation/rearm. Reuse the real keyguard material/painter with current mode, scope/category, data, palette, geometry, density, labels where applicable, disclosure configuration and a defined continuation phase. Count as READY only after pixel production is complete. Use a bounded single latest desired job, one ready entry with lease-safe retirement, a monotonic generation and exact identity. Late A1 may never replace A2 after A/B/A updates. Persist no FULL pixels to disk. Readiness is permission to retain an app-private image in RAM; a separate current decision is required to expose it.

Avoid deriving an always-changing animation-time key independently at lookup. Adopt the prepared image's phase and start the live animation from it; use a separately captured phase when required by existing continuity. Retire outputs and revoke reveal rights on every seal. An inactive image may survive an ordinary window withdrawal only while all original data-access/retention rules still allow it. Purge it on privacy/data-access revocation, user/account change, disable, relevant expiry, process/service disposal and memory pressure. Ordinary internal images have no WindowManager/SurfaceControl parent or attached surface; never pre-submit private pixels to an attached transparent or hidden display surface. No detached ticker, wake lock or continuous background service.

If the new request is not yet available, leave the registered obligation pending and schedule when actually offered without waiting on an obsolete positive's Main disposal. Preserve queue progress if a coroutine, worker or Main task is cancelled.

Only this provably empty path may discard obsolete positive work. Forward already observed exclusions, system-off/unknown, user switch, disconnect, queued restrictive action and any prior owner requiring withdrawal through existing ordered restriction handling first. Carry the outstanding cache-clear/freshness obligation until the proper physical call establishes it. An ordinary equal-value publication should not invalidate the same reservation. ### 10. Warm presentation and animation

On a warm hit deliver the already prepared private image through the actual stock opening entry point. Prepare the app-private image, eligible empty host and independent current-scene read in parallel. Once the exact host is ready and a fresh FULL decision is available, submit the poster without first waiting for a live painter or making the owner wait for the first live worker post. Preserve the ordering of restrictions throughout any delay to that submit.

On the supported DIRECT path use a dedicated non-interactive poster child in the existing owner, with a distinct live BufferQueue child. Bind the private composed buffer plus intended visibility/geometry on a single authorized SurfaceControl transaction. Do not call setBuffer on the layer that owns the live Surface producer. Prepare the compatible HardwareBuffer off the hot path, with COMPOSER_OVERLAY and GPU_SAMPLED_IMAGE usage plus render-target usage if required, alpha/color space/crop and completed producer fence. Do not assume any arbitrary hardware Bitmap buffer qualifies. Keep display/release-fence ownership and leases bounded, including on abort, replacement and dispose. At first valid live continuation atomically switch visibility from poster to live in the same owner; retain the poster until the actual correctly phased live buffer is ready. Static/reduced-motion mode may keep just the poster. If that buffer format/permission is unsupported, implement a real stock fallback that blits the prepared bitmap once via the existing authorized surface before starting the live scene. This fallback still implements private preparation and the revised reader; log its extra post separately. A cold/missing/stale image uses the existing safe normal render path and schedules the next prepare. Never pause the clock or hold the system screen to wait for Fluvi.

Android public API reference: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/SurfaceControl.Transaction#setBuffer(android.view.SurfaceControl,android.hardware.HardwareBuffer,android.hardware.SyncFence,java.util.function.Consumer)

### 11. Release and withdrawal races

Own every displayed child and pending submit under one generation. Invalidate pending work on restriction; cancel unreached submits, order hide/unparent of both visible owners on the presentation lane, and prevent stale queued poster/live callbacks from restoring either child. Cover restriction between scalar admission, native submission and its receipt. Distinguish a command that was queued, submitted, committed or visibly withdrawn. Never claim to undo a previously submitted frame retroactively. Cache eviction must not invalidate buffers still leased by the compositor. Do not defer the restrictive action behind resource release, fence waiting or the live transition. Keep the existing fail-closed fallback when host/bind/disposal fails.

## 2026-11-23 — R35 design decision. Put the prepared ORB in the first ordinary clock frame

FLUVI_R35_FIRST_CLOCK_FRAME_BEGIN

### 1. TITLE / TASK INTENT

IMPLEMENTATION handoff. The owner wants at most 10 ms of *visible* lag. Replace the dependency on Fluvi doing work at wake. While data/settings change, Fluvi publishes the configured material to a trusted primary lockscreen display owner. Before sleep that owner has the actual ready-to-draw image. When composing the first eligible main clock frame it draws its current image at the saved position. On the first restricted frame it excludes that image. Live animation may start afterward. This entry supersedes the reader-cancellation continuation in the preceding R34 handset review as the primary repair. That review's evidence remains applicable.

### 2. AUTHORITATIVE APPLICATION STATE

The preferred milestone's four app-wake-to-native-return times were 356/407/342/320 ms. Its actual worker paint/post cost only 2.25–8.42 ms. The milestone already paid for a post-wake authorization. R34 demonstrably cached pixels; it retained this dependency. The measurements are separate sessions. The two obsolete-read suffixes of 207/161 ms are evidence for a compatibility-path optimization only. Even two winning complete reads alone took 48/55 ms. The R34 black privacy panel still showed FULL after REDACTED on the older isolated renderer. Treat the existing APK and any unqualified candidate as demo-data diagnostics. The reference README describes a staged, disabled bootstrap. Its presence in a checkout or packaged app does not install a host on a factory OS.

### 7. GRAPH PROVENANCE AND IMPACT

Exact app graph manifest at b329107c8a9c387c513151afec1b658ac732942b records source e41485b4, parent b63a829d and Dart SCIP 1.6.2. Use that graph for existing settings and data mutation producers. Review native Android and platform Kotlin directly. Impacted existing owners are R29PublisherSnapshot, R29HostClient, R29Ownership/Store, R29ResidentStore, R29HostRenderer/R29PreparedOrb, R29FramePolicy, FluviOrbHostService and the legacy final submit path for exclusive ownership. Inspect the actual host's active clock renderer. On the pinned reference it is reached through LockscreenContent.Content, the selected DefaultBlueprint.Content and DefaultClockLayout; preserve the full root coordinate space for ORB geometry.

### 8. CURRENT SOURCE FACTS

R34 advanceR19First waits for a current main-keyguard result, the matching owner/output and a valid disclosure before its DIRECT overlay can submit the prepared image. The R29 reference has a small authenticated descriptor protocol, a worker preparation path, a RAM-resident image and poster-first drawing. Its app publisher is not connected to production updates. REQUEST_EMPTY invalidates and the client currently ignores CALLBACK_EMPTY. Its enrollment, source projection, acceptable display geometry and blueprint are limited. Its current() and first draw require inspection for locking, repeated validation, allocation and first-use upload. The existing host resets on a numeric trim threshold that can include UI_HIDDEN. Exercise real sleep transitions and real memory pressure separately.

### 9. PROVEN / UNPROVEN / MISSING

A full AppWidgetManager.updateAppWidget can populate the system widget cache. It does not select the factory primary clock composition. Android 15 and 17 CDD §3.8.2 make lockscreen widgets optional, and the Android Developers FAQ leaves experience triggers to the OEM. A public widget in an auxiliary hub, a notification, a wallpaper and a window-level accessibility attachment offer different visibility, security or interaction semantics. Eligibility for private data also requires an authenticated destination. The identified stock interface gives no universal factory-phone 10 ms guarantee. Only an actual supported primary host with the required scene, restriction and placement semantics can qualify its retail configuration. A whole-window attachment, widget category, installed package, OEM name or API-level check cannot establish this capability.

### 10. ROOT-CAUSE OR FORENSIC GATE

The first-frame dependency belongs to the wrong owner. The app infers the current screen after it wakes. Move current-scene authority and resource ownership together to the component already composing that screen. The decisive negative control is an already prepared R34 image with Fluvi suspended before wake: the app cannot make a new overlay submission. The positive control is a real primary host rendering the accepted generation while Fluvi remains suspended, with zero required app-side events between wake and the first ORB. A fast cached read, stale remembered FULL result or existing previous-frame overlay cannot satisfy that control.

### 11. SCOPE LOCK / NO-TOUCH

The deliverable for retail remains an ordinary APK on the existing OS. Keep the existing overlay as separately identified compatibility behavior and compare to de807259. Do not auto-enable it over an enrolled strict host, switch the user's wallpaper, add a replacement lockscreen, alter the dashboard/home widget or change the meaning of FULL. Retain current product interaction behavior and test it on the chosen owner. An equivalent OEM integration can be used on systems that offer it. A test-only host is appropriate to test publication now. Paired SystemUI integration is separately scoped reference engineering, never a phone upgrade instruction. No device flashing, root, private-API bypass, production platform-signing request, paid runner procurement or external OEM outreach is part of this handoff.

### 12. LAYERS / BOUNDS / OWNERSHIP

One coherent, immutable image generation per user, display, material, data, geometry and privacy revision. One actual primary presentation owner. Start with the existing data-only wire representation where it describes the actual configured ORB. The trusted receiver can render the exact poster once at update time and retain it privately. Keep raw transactions/amount labels and executable rendering code out of the wire payload. Widen currently unsupported product modes using verified source provenance or mark them unavailable. Never silently substitute a default image. Adopt an already uploaded or otherwise demonstrably draw-ready resource for the active display. Track expiry, coherent wall-clock/date changes, theme, scale, display changes, revocation, user switch and process restart. Host-visible validity changes invalidate old FULL at their commit boundary. Make update/revoke ordering explicit across both ends; deny a stale image when freshness cannot be established. Ordinary app sleep after acknowledged clean detachment preserves only the accepted, still-valid generation. Unexpected death mid-update retains the existing fail-closed semantics. Genuine host memory loss, boot before credentials unlock, eviction and expiry are measured misses.

### 13. REQUIRED RED TESTS

Use normal publication entry points. Drive a genuine palette/scope or demo balance revision; the parent must fail to deliver the correct changed generation to an independently running receiver. Verify READY identifies observed image B after A, repeated identical content, delayed obsolete A and privacy revocation. Test publisher death before and after clean detachment, host restart and empty acknowledgement with the wrong token. On a true primary host, render clock-only control → cached ORB in the same eligible frame while app is suspended → first PIN/shade/unlock frame containing zero FULL pixels. Inspect transitions that retain outgoing layers. Negative controls include stale imagery, a second overlay, a hub page, a hidden/delayed clock, a generic blob and a later live repaint. Keep these failures distinguishable from unavailable test setup.

### 14. IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT

1. Publish from the actual data/settings update pipeline while Fluvi is running, including cold initial sync, changes to mode, scope/category, palette, geometry, permissions and date. Deduplicate by coherent source revision. Prepare in advance of locking; the lock/screen-off callback can verify readiness but cannot be the sole trigger. Verify the remote endpoint and enrollment before disclosing private material. Return an independently produced READY receipt for the exact generation only after render readiness. Use the current exclusive-ownership transition and complete the matching EMPTY acknowledgement before permitting another output owner.
2. In the strict path remove the app's wake callback, Flutter, storage, shader compilation, accessibility tree walk, new window, Binder round trip and live worker from the dependencies for first visible content. The host's frame reads an already validated immutable slot and its own authoritative scene/epoch. Eligible plus current draws the prepared resource; otherwise the scene contains no FULL orb. Keep this operation bounded, with no application restart or wait and no delaying the clock. An existing callback may run for unrelated purposes but must not be required to present or remove content.
3. The first restricted frame owns exclusion of both static and animated orb and their interaction regions, including a crossfade, shade, bouncer, going-away or a new user. A persisted old-frame screenshot, surface or delayed callback must not resurrect FULL. Replace or suppress outgoing visuals at the common scene/composition boundary. An EMPTY acknowledgement references the correct owner, generation and completed no-ORB output, independent of onDraw/command return. Start live animation later from the precomputed first-frame phase in the same owner. Preserve reduced motion, no blank frame, no repeated first-frame flash, no interference with normal keyguard input.
4. For a **separately selected reference build**, reuse the pinned Android 16 frameworks/base 99b01a65cc4c104933788b3143285ab6bae65827. Integrate in the active primary blueprint's clock traversal with the real scene transition and scrim owners. Confirm which implementation and feature flags the booted image actually uses. Wire the prebuilt slot into the existing root, below restrictive UI. A patched but inactive file, standalone Activity or detached test surface cannot establish this. Keep the existing reference's debug/signer protections and preserve factory installation behavior.

### 15. PERFORMANCE GATE

Record W = physical wake stimulus, C = first visible eligible ordinary clock, O = first visible *correct configured* ORB, R = start of a restrictive transition, and last observable FULL. Primary score is O−C, inclusive maximum 10 ms. Keep W→O, O→first distinct motion and R→last FULL independent. If AOD is already showing a clock, use the qualified AOD-to-ordinary transition; record biometric bypass with no ordinary frame and require no FULL. Include every attempted wake, with missed, cold, unsupported and indeterminate cases counted separately; a missing ORB is a failed eligible trial. Never hold the clock to improve O−C. Use an independent optical reference for acceptance, not an app timer. Establish a measurement uncertainty interval per trial with calibrated camera/optical timing, correct image regions, panel scanout and camera exposure. Upper bound ≤10 ms passes timing; lower bound >10 ms fails; an interval crossing 10 is indeterminate. At 60 Hz one missed refresh is approximately 16.7 ms. A common frame is the design target, not a substitute for optical evidence.

### 16. IMPLEMENTATION ORDER

First land an end-to-end working publisher and an instrumented, authenticated test receiver using the real app update path and a scene-rendered demo image, including the empty handover. Start this work even when the retail interface is absent. Mark that milestone PUBLISHER/RECEIVER VERIFIED only. In parallel qualify a specifically identified retail host independently of the test receiver; use existing published capability evidence and enroll only with normal owner opt-in. If a real suitable host exists, implement the adapter and test the complete stock path. If none is available, keep the strict retail route unavailable and complete and return all independent work, exact source, repeatable tests and blocker. Provide the deployable paired-host reference plan independently. Do not turn a missing retail integration into a claim of device support or a reason to stop after a documentation scan.

### 17. VALIDATION

Run the existing Android build/verification lane for app code, focused production Kotlin/Flutter bridge tests and real instrumentation with package/signature checks and two processes. Use a normal API 35 test install for publisher and compatibility controls and retain exact route identities. Run steady wake, AOD, cold run, process suspension after acknowledgement, quick unlock/relock, PIN, both privacy panel backgrounds, shade/QS, stale data, configuration changes, unsupported host and live handover. Compare eligible clock onset to an ORB-disabled control. Record refresh rate without forcing it for the main result. Test available 60/90/120 Hz variants and supported versions separately. Report actual completed counts, screenshots/trace per eligible transition and the physical upper bound. Report red or incomplete privacy cases. The existing reference platform qualification requires actual Soong-compiled SystemUI and a booted matched reference target; an APK emulator or JVM harness cannot qualify it.

### 18. COMMIT DISCIPLINE

Keep app code, fixture-only changes, optional platform reference and append-only coordination evidence identifiable. Preserve the exact app and test-source SHAs and the two comparison APKs' source identities. Reference user-private logs by capture ID and timings, with synthetic demo data for screenshots.

### 19. PUSH / BUILD / GRAPH REGENERATION

Use the existing verified build/sign/download workflow for an app or test artifact whose behavior actually changed. Produce a repeatable publisher/receiver instrumentation deliverable where available. A factory-phone APK qualifies as an owner latency candidate only if there is an identified working adapter target for that phone; label everything else by its actual purpose. Verify package signature/update, source SHA, checksum and download. Refresh exact-candidate Dart graph and native inventory for application changes. Describe OS-side reference artifacts separately if that work is selected. No new retail repair APK is represented by this design entry.

### 20. COMPLETION REPORT

Return implementation commits and verified artifacts; the actual recipient of the prepared image; preparation time relative to wake; generation, scene, frame and output ownership; count of app calls required between wake and first ORB; matching exclusion/EMPTY frame; distribution and maxima with missed/unknown counts; source, host, display, OS and optical method; compatibility and privacy status. Minimal per-trial probing only. Report publisher-only, reference, retail path and physical phone acceptance independently. The owner already supplied sufficient logs to start.

### 21. DEFINITION OF DONE

For a specified factory configuration, the qualified feature requires the ordinary clock and current configured ORB in the first eligible composition with Fluvi suspended, zero FULL in the first restricted composition, the original placements/interactions, no deferred clock, and physical upper bound ≤10 ms on every measured eligible trial. A tested configuration can qualify; universal support cannot be inferred. If the factory OS offers no suitable display integration, the truthful result is that the requested universal product cannot be delivered by a standalone APK under these constraints. Keep the milestone as the opening comparator and the prior privacy findings open until independently resolved.

* The accepted native material-store path now exposes a frozen visual profile and the supplied Flutter provenance to an explicitly installed R35 publisher consumer. Relevant producers are `lib/app/platform/dashboard_keyguard_material_bridge.dart:88,104,106,163`, `android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/MainActivity.kt:1215,1231`, and `lockscreen/material/KeyguardMaterialProfile.kt:335,344`. Settings/layout changes notify that consumer before their writes (`lockscreen/KeyguardCardSettings.kt:199,263`). The consumer is absent by default and **there is no production constructor/activation call for `R35ResidentPublisher`**. This hook is not an enrolled or working retail path.
* `lockscreen/host/R35ResidentPublisher.kt` is a staged, explicitly invoked adapter: after an authenticated session it asks the actual Flutter producer for fresh provenance, resolves the current native Budget projection, revision, settings and geometry, and sends the existing bounded data-only descriptor through `R29HostClient`. Unsupported or unproven projections do not become FULL. The current Flutter evidence path is limited to a verified Budget-category projection; other product modes are not qualified. Full cold-start sync, all update sources, deduplication, transport failure and atomic host-visible revocation are **not yet demonstrated**. The normal Android overlay remains the active factory route.
* `R29HostClient` now accepts an EMPTY callback only from its authenticated active sender when session, sequence and persistent owner epoch match the outstanding request. Its true return from `requestEmpty` means queued only. `R29Ownership` rejects a disconnect from an old epoch. The existing reference service `platform/aosp16/systemui/src/com/android/systemui/keyguard/fluvi/FluviOrbHostService.kt:182` still only invalidates: it does **not** issue a real completed primary-frame EMPTY. Admission/final-submission gates for an actual host and the exclusive-owner handover are not wired. Do not enable this path as a retail feature.
* A debug-build-only, same-UID, non-exported, separately running service is added at `android/app/src/debug/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen/host/R35DebugResidentService.kt`. It uses the reference renderer and an ImageReader test surface; its potential EMPTY receipt refers only to that offscreen demo buffer. The API35 instrumented A/B test is present at `android/app/src/androidTest/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen/host/R35ResidentPublisherInstrumentationTest.kt`, but **has not run**. No debug receiver or test surface is a primary-clock host. No app-suspension, first-clock-frame, restricted-frame or physical timing result is claimed.
* The separate reference memory policy no longer treats `TRIM_MEMORY_UI_HIDDEN` as low-memory eviction. The actual reference SystemUI service source calls this policy; no patched system image has been built or booted. Its current resident read still performs locking/validation, and its temporary GPU warm-up is not proof of first-frame residency.

### R35 factory primary-lockscreen capability check — 2026-11-24

Task: the owner's R35 continuation at `6d5ba6ecb573377ffc871d7222dc5d48af731533`, restricted to `elizerpist/exptv2`. The current application/test branch `implement/r35-first-clock-frame` is `c1d1c552315618e24a224b8dae6ef26852e48d03` and the worktree is clean. Its only changes since production candidate `1393e8c5023065f2930b67c9c4a95f78c8d1473c` are debug/instrumentation/CI files; no stock display integration was added. Prior [R35 run 45343583422](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/actions/runs/45343583422) verifies A/B/EMPTY on a separately running **debug-only ImageReader**, not on a lockscreen.

Direct source checks: `android/app/src/main/res/xml/fluvi_orb_widget_info.xml` declares the ORB `home_screen`; `fluvi_financial_snapshot_widget_info.xml` is a different provider declaring `home_screen|keyguard`. Provider declarations are not a diagnosis of any particular picker and neither establishes the first primary-clock frame. The `R35DebugResidentService` is declared only in `android/app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml`, and the only call constructing `R35ResidentPublisher` is in `R35ResidentPublisherInstrumentationTest.kt`. The staged production `R29HostClient` expects the exported, platform-signed `com.android.systemui.keyguard.fluvi.FluviOrbHostService`; that app-specific service file is absent from the inspected [pinned AOSP16 SystemUI source](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/99b01a65cc4c104933788b3143285ab6bae65827/packages/SystemUI/src/com/android/systemui/keyguard/) (parent directory HTTP 200, `fluvi/FluviOrbHostService.kt` HTTP 404). This AOSP check is not an inspection of Nothing's proprietary firmware.

The public [Android 15 CDD §3.8.2](https://source.android.com/docs/compatibility/15/android-15-cdd#382_widgets) says an implementation **may** support app widgets on the lock screen; the [Android widget API](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/appwidget/AppWidgetProviderInfo) exposes categories but does not guarantee a host in the primary clock composition. Google's [2025 lockscreen widget FAQ](https://android-developers.googleblog.com/2025/03/widgets-on-lock-screen-faq.html) states that the experience and its triggers are OEM-dependent and describes later AOSP availability; it also says all widgets are compatible with that later experience unless opted out. Thus `home_screen` alone is not proof that a particular OEM picker must exclude the ORB, and existence of an auxiliary widget surface does not establish the required same-clock-frame contract.

`adb devices -l` returned no attached device. The owner previously identified a Nothing A142/API35 handset, but its current exact firmware and actual primary-lockscreen host were not observable in this environment. A search of available Nothing support documentation did not identify a compatible public primary-clock host contract; this is **not proof that no OEM-specific implementation exists**. No APK was installed, no physical frame was measured, and no real user data was displayed.

**Result: STOCK PRIMARY HOST — NOT ESTABLISHED.** The missing capability is a supported, authenticated system-owned primary-lockscreen integration that can retain the correct configured ORB while Fluvi is suspended, compose it with the first eligible ordinary clock frame without delaying that clock, and omit it in the first PIN/shade/unlock restricted frame with correct ownership and privacy. A widget category flag or the test receiver does not establish that capability. In accordance with the continuation, no provider was relabelled, no production code was changed, no new APK/CI run was produced, and no 10 ms result was claimed. A suitable documented OEM contract or an on-device synthetic observation of the actual primary-screen binding is needed before selecting an adapter. The known R34 privacy-panel failure and physical acceptance remain open. **PHYSICAL VALIDATION — PENDING, USER ONLY.**

Send a complete RemoteViews update at registration/binding or configuration and suitable lifecycle updates, with no periodic timer or wake receiver required to reveal the prepared image. The host retains the last delivered state. Make it possible for the user to find the trial and recognize its image after install, including after opening Fluvi once. Avoid requiring a pre-existing financial database or changing system settings. If recording diagnostics, keep only non-sensitive provider update/binding facts; an update callback or reported host category cannot establish appearance.

### 15. PERFORMANCE GATE
Score first ordinary clock pixels to first *correct* visible trial ORB, maximum 10 ms inclusive. Separate initial discoverability and placement from display timing. Count loops where the clock appears and the ORB is missing or late. Keep wake stimulus→ORB, animation if measured, and PIN/shade/unlock disappearance separate. Manual inspection detects obvious lag; a precise claim requires measurements with uncertainty bounds sufficient for 10 ms. Never delay the clock. A static demo isolates first appearance and does not qualify full live-animation parity or financial privacy.

### 16. IMPLEMENTATION ORDER
Implement and commit the provider/assets. Verify merged profile content and exercise the provider against a framework host where available. Immediately start the pinned exptv2 phone builder and continue through signing, obtaining the APK, publication and download verification. Run independent tests alongside the build. If a recoverable runner or source failure occurs, fix and retry in exptv2. Once an installable artifact is qualified as a diagnostic build, deliver it even when the handset observation is pending.

### 17. VALIDATION
Confirm package ID, version, signer and required ABI/Android support. Build and inspect the exact artifact, check with apksigner and aapt/apkanalyzer and verify the additional widget label/provider appears in the HUMAN package. Install/update on a compatible Android test target if available. Record what was tested on an emulator and what remains for the user. Test normal launch after install plus the widget control where a host exists. Ensure an existing Fluvi installation/user data are not placed at risk by the test instructions.

### 18. COMMIT DISCIPLINE
Keep app source, build/tooling and downloadable binary identities separate and pinned. The coding agent owns code commits, binary signing, build, publication and execution report. Append evidence to the common journal on fix/orb-v4-latency-lockscreen. Keep short checkpoints if a lengthy build is in progress. No unrelated workflow, repository or project changes.

### 19. PUSH / BUILD / GRAPH REGENERATION
Use the existing exptv2 phone diagnostic builder or equivalent established exptv2 build lane with an exact application SHA and scripts/build-human-diagnostic-apk.sh. A CI-signed intermediate is not automatically update-compatible. Verify its signer against the installed series (R34 certificate SHA-256 faedbe8483532ebb1412bf4d8387c36ff6bbcd4b1da560ba0eabbaea9bad49fb); use the authorized existing phone signing process. If that signer is genuinely unavailable, build the **same Fluvi candidate** as a clearly labelled, separately installable diagnostic variant with its own application ID and signer, verify any authorities/provider component IDs and native assumptions, and label it as side-by-side. Never tell the owner to uninstall Fluvi or erase data. Refresh applicable exact-source graph/native inventory under the established workflow; do not conflate graph SHA with app SHA. Publish the real .apk with a directly downloadable exptv2 release asset or verified binary URL, not a workflow page, ZIP, LFS pointer or expired link.

### 20. COMPLETION REPORT
First line: direct signed APK download. Include source SHA, APK byte count, SHA-256, signing/install mode, and a successful re-download with matching bytes. Follow with three phone steps: (1) install, open once, identify the new test by name/color and turn off the old overlay for this trial if enabled; (2) look specifically in the phone's **primary lockscreen** widget picker and place the demo if offered; (3) lock/wake several times and report whether it appears with the clock, only after swiping, late, or not at all; check PIN/shade/unlock with only demo content. The owner can report “not listed” without enabling the old overlay. If the phone cannot place it, record that result with firmware/host context without generalizing to every device.

### 21. DEFINITION OF DONE
Delivery for this assignment is a changed, verified, directly downloadable installable Fluvi diagnostic APK plus brief handset instructions. Device admission and optical ≤10 ms are subsequent validation outcomes, separately reported. An artifactless source checkpoint or a capability report does not complete this assignment. If a true external blocker prevents delivery after the authorized build/signing alternatives, name the exact failed operation and retained evidence; do not claim a phone fix.

The old positive may only be superseded after completion. Android calls already in flight cannot be treated as cancelled. KeyguardSurfaceClassifier prioritizes restrictive/unknown conditions over clock markers; a partial positive cannot authorize the financial image.

### 9. PROVEN / UNPROVEN / MISSING

The observed lag precedes the fast poster submit. Some of the work finishing after a new scene can be removed on stock Android. The start and duration of the winning full read, the host time and display composition can remain limiting; winning complete reads on the current phone report include 34 and 27 ms. The architecture below is an evidence-backed attempt to shorten the actual opening. It does not establish a universal or physical 10 ms result. An owner-visible APK is required to measure its effect. Keep sparse traces, misses and phone reports separate from fixture evidence.

### 10. ROOT-CAUSE DECISION

For eligible empty DIRECT openings use a single current physical reader with one replaceable genuine successor. Move **obsolete-work disposal** earlier; leave **positive permission** with the fresh, complete decision. Capture the initial reservation and generation before the first framework inventory, independent of whether Main has published the final R34 owner yet. Resolve that same reservation against the adopted owner later only if uninterrupted emptiness and identity can be established. This removes wasted traversal and Main-dispatch work for superseded reads. It does not manufacture authority from an old wake or merely appearing clock text. If evidence of continuous ownership is unavailable in a path, use the verified adopted-owner optimization there or keep the existing behavior.

### 11. SCOPE LOCK / NO-TOUCH

The change must execute by default through the existing **Fluvi-kártya a zárképernyőn → Csak orb** normal entry on the eligible route. Retain all currently supported compatibility routes, opt-out and reduced motion. No testing toggle required on the owner's phone. No changes to widget admission, AOSP, wallpaper, dashboard, financial DB or data seeding. No generic placeholder, deliberate clock delay, double overlay or always-visible financial buffer. Do not skip a new permission grant, soften an exclusion or trust a prior lock's FULL state for latency.

### 12. LAYERS / BOUNDS / OWNERSHIP

Use a small immutable reservation stamp or reuse the equivalent existing token, with original request, authority, owner/route identity, inventory scene and freshness. Proof of emptiness must cover any old visible owner, held submit/paint/grant, pending restriction and outstanding drain capable of displaying previous content. A newly allocated slot alone is insufficient. Capture/update scalar state under the existing queue lock. Keep Android calls, recycling, trace formatting and drawing outside it. Maintain one physical reader and one publishable result; avoid another queue or periodic retry. Never attach an original read to a different owner after a rapid relock, even when scalar values match.

### 13. REQUIRED RED TESTS

Use the real service, queue and reader hooks in an isolated Android test. (A) During actual active-root acquisition inject a genuine newer event, return the call while old descendants remain, and count further Android calls for that obsolete request. (B) Repeat at a per-window root, last child/leaf and on a read started before Main adopts the identical empty reservation. (C) Inject B then C and check the genuine latest request runs exactly once, with bounded single-reader concurrency. Count stale calls on the parent and candidate under the same schedule. Also test no pending offer, delayed offer, wrong generation/ABA, overlapping native retire, owner replacement, foreground transition, coroutine cancellation and shutdown. A timeout before a stale read or before a matching eventual winner is NOT REACHED, not proof of a fix. Use a test-only fixture overlay when comparing the parent and retain its original production code.

### 14. IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT

1. Put the selected zero-disclosure opening under a single tracked scheduling path from its initial reservation. Preserve the before-inventory scene stamp across adoption. For exact-owner promotion, prove the same reservation/epochs, revisions and absence of outgoing or incoming private pixels over the interval. Leave unprovable cases on the established conservative path and record the reason in compact diagnostics.
2. At a returned window inventory, active root, per-window root and each returned child (including final child/leaf), and before the next expensive framework access or final submission of a result, check whether continuing the read can still produce an applicable result. Keep the fast unchanged case inexpensive; a generation hint may avoid taking the lock. Revalidate under the authoritative queue lock before transferring. Treat already observed restrictive evidence, ambiguous ownership and outstanding freshness/clear obligations in their proper order. Wire the checks also where batch prefetch is unavailable. Release each node/root and unwind resources exactly once on the correct thread.
3. Require a genuine newer compatible pending request with matching authority, current scene, default display and event provenance. Atomically retire obsolete work and claim the latest pending request. Only after the old physical reader unwinds may the new one enter Android. A stale early cancellation is its own typed result; do not let it publish FULL, produce an artificial restrictive transition or erase a real negative. If no eligible successor can be claimed, preserve progress with existing ordered handling; do not introduce a new timer, open-ended parking or synthetic proof. On a stream of actual changes stay hidden while a complete proof is unavailable; after it settles the latest full valid read must progress to display.
4. Retain the already prepared poster, host preparation, final live state check, one-use proof, reveal/withdrawal ordering and animation continuation on the existing owner. A current, complete positive takes the existing normal path. Test shade, PIN, foreign occlusion and quick unlock arriving during unwind, after proof and before native submit. If no measurable saving exists, still deliver the safe changed diagnostic for handset testing with accurate results.

### 15. PERFORMANCE GATE

Count all test attempts and all eligible wakes, including misses. In LIGHT store bounded per-attempt data: source SHA, normal route, original read/scene, first real superseding offer, Android-call return and boundary, claim or precise fallback reason, obsolete post-boundary calls, latest reader start, full read end, proof/grant, poster submit/return, first motion and withdrawal. Preserve existing limits and omit sensitive content. Primary software outcomes: fewer obsolete Android calls, earlier start of the winning scan, earlier permission, earlier native submit on matched runs. Report per-attempt durations, maxima and any regression. They are distinct from clock-to-first-correct-visible-ORB ≤10 ms, which requires a physical observation at sufficient precision. Do not make a camera, an OEM widget or proof of the 10 ms ceiling a prerequisite for APK delivery.

### 16. IMPLEMENTATION ORDER

Create the meaningful production diff and regression controls, pass focused local checks, commit and push a pinned application SHA. Start the exact-SHA HUMAN build as soon as compile and core safety checks allow. Run the independent validation lanes in parallel with packaging. Remain responsible through build, signing, publication and verifying the downloaded bytes. Monitor runs to terminal status and repair recoverable Gradle/Maven, checkout, runner space, emulator, signing or upload failures within exptv2. If a correction changes application code, rebuild, republish and verify against the corrected SHA. Intermediate plans, test results, links to Actions jobs and promises to build later are progress updates only.

### 17. VALIDATION

Run diff/boundary checks, app/core unit regressions, Android compile, focused single-reader/recovery and exact service instrumentation, then the repository's normal independent qualification. Exercise the simplest user entry: enabled normal card, ORB/orbOnly, FULL demo material, lock, wake, unlock, rapid relock. Require cause-correlated original/obsolete/winning IDs and a visible ordinary ORB in the instrumented control. Preserve black/white privacy sample controls, pending submit reversal and process/owner replacement cases; report pending and known failures expressly. Use the validated exptv2 builder and APK upgrade control. Compare the actual installed R36 and R37 on the same emulator settings in alternating order if supported. No reversal of the user's settings or resetting the database to obtain a green test.

### 18. COMMIT DISCIPLINE

All source, tests, build jobs, signed artifacts and journal records stay in elizerpist/exptv2. Keep test harness changes identifiable. The new application SHA must include the normal service change; app binary must carry it and invoke it along an ordinary opening. Preserve the existing milestone and old APKs. Track any signing material according to its existing secure handling, outside commits. The reviewer only appends this handoff to the coordination journal.

### 19. PUSH / BUILD / GRAPH REGENERATION

Use the proven exptv2 orchestration/r36-phone-builder at adf5e319bf2cab92e8653e4e8024f3584833c054, workflow fluvi-core.yml, dispatch on the orchestration ref with app_sha=<full changed application SHA>. Precedent: successful R36 builder run 45351890685. Preserve the HUMAN profile script and default disabled demo-database seeding. Use the established handset signing/publication procedure; verify correct package com.fluvi.app and update signer SHA-256 faedbe8483532ebb1412bf4d8387c36ff6bbcd4b1da560ba0eabbaea9bad49fb. Test install -r over the actual signed R36 in a disposable test target, keep a sentinel and verify Activity resumed. If the same signer proves genuinely unavailable after using the existing authorized path, deliver a clearly labeled, separately installable **full Fluvi** HUMAN diagnostic built from the changed normal path; ensure distinct application ID/authorities, correct self-overlay attribution, Android service registration, side-by-side install and ordinary display exercised. Preserve the existing install/data and explicitly identify any limitations of such an alternate. No widget-only, debug instrumentation or repackaged old APK is a deliverable.

Publish a direct stable exptv2 binary URL (same immutable LFS-media or verified release pattern as R36; for example a distinct fluvi_R37_HUMAN_<source>.apk). Download it independently in full, follow redirects, check HTTP status, byte count, APK/ZIP format, package, signer and SHA-256 against the signed output. A Git LFS text pointer, temporary CI ZIP or successful upload response alone fails delivery. Keep code graph/native inventory current and separate its identity from the app SHA. Preserve the usable download throughout qualification.

### 20. COMPLETION REPORT

First line: direct verified download link for the **new R37 APK**. Then source commit, byte count, hash, signing/update mode and one sentence describing the actual changed wake path. Give a three-step Hungarian phone test: install/update and open once; use the usual animated ORB on the main lockscreen with the same settings as R36 and demo content (no widget picker); lock/wake several times and rapidly unlock once, reporting appearance alongside the clock and disappearance. Provide the run/qualification links, route evidence and measured results with the 10 ms physical status stated separately. Append the same artifact identity and limits to this journal.

### 21. DEFINITION OF DONE

The coding agent's delivery condition is a **changed, signed, installable and independently downloadable normal animated-ORB APK** in the owner's hands, with exact identity and phone instructions. Do not end at a merge, checkpoint, CI failure, successful test, successful compile or local APK. Continue authorized recovery and finish package delivery. The owner performs the physical acceptance afterward. A failure to demonstrate a physical 10 ms ceiling is recorded as pending or failed as appropriate and does not delay the phone build. Do not ship a known new privacy bypass to satisfy delivery; fix or conservatively disable the unsafe subcase while retaining and exercising the safe production change.

**Coding-agent correction.** Keep W (physical switch actuation), L (first identifiable light from the waking display), C (first eligible main clock) and O (first correct on-screen ORB) distinguishable.
